articles.title: VIDEO: nuvem de poeira chama a atenção durante vendaval no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo foi registrado em Campo Mourão, na tarde de sexta-feira (20). Segundo o Simepar, os ventos atingiram 79,9 km/h.
articles.summary: Vídeo foi registrado em Campo Mourão, na tarde de sexta-feira (20). Segundo o Simepar, os ventos atingiram 79,9 km/h.
articles.body:
Uma nuvem de poeira foi registrada durante um vendaval em Campo Mourão , no centro-oeste do Paraná, na tarde de sexta-feira (20). Assista acima.

As imagens mostram a nuvem se formando e avançando com a força do vento. Deorque Frederico, autor do vídeo, contou à RPC , afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, que passeava com alguns amigos pelo lago da usina quando a chuva chegou. O grupo levou um susto, mas ninguém ficou ferido.

Segundo o Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar), uma rajada de vento atingiu 79,9 km/h por volta das 17h45, em Campo Mourão.

O vendaval também provocou estragos na cidade. Uma árvore caiu sobre uma casa e danificou o imóvel. Houve ainda relatos de quedas de árvores, danos em telhados e obstrução de vias.

Por volta das 22h de sexta, cerca de 12,6 mil unidades consumidoras estavam sem energia elétrica, segundo consulta ao painel da Companhia Paranaense de Energia (Copel).

articles.title: Veja traje da brasileira no Miss Universo 2026, inspirado no guaraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Traje reúne mais de 40 mil cristais, iluminação em LED, 'frutos' de impressão 3D e folhas feitas com garrafas PET recicladas. Produção mobilizou mais de 25 profissionais.
articles.summary: Traje reúne mais de 40 mil cristais, iluminação em LED, 'frutos' de impressão 3D e folhas feitas com garrafas PET recicladas. Produção mobilizou mais de 25 profissionais.
articles.body:
Brasileira no Miss Universo 2026, Marcella Kozinski usa traje inspirado no guaraná — Foto: Gabriel Amilkar /Palmer Assessoria de Comunicação

Marcella Kozinski, representante do Brasil no Miss Universo 2026 , escolheu o guaraná como símbolo do país para o desfile de trajes típicos, que ocorre neste sábado (21), em Porto Rico.

A peça, assinada pelo figurinista Bruno Oliveira, foi intitulada de "Guaraná, o fruto sagrado da terra" e reúne mais de 40 mil cristais, iluminação em LED, frutos produzidos em impressão 3D e folhas confeccionadas a partir de garrafas PET recicladas.

"Homenagear o guaraná já era um desejo meu. É um fruto da nossa terra, e poder levá-lo ao palco do Miss Universo é uma forma de compartilhar nossas raízes com o mundo. Espero que as pessoas se encantem com o traje e queiram conhecer mais sobre o guaraná e sobre a riqueza da natureza brasileira", afirma Marcella.

➡️👁️‍🗨️ O guaraná é uma planta nativa da Amazônia e o Brasil é maior produtor comercial do fruto no mundo. Pequeno, avermelhado ou alaranjado, quando maduro, se abre revelando sementes escuras parcialmente cobertas por uma película branca. Dessa forma, a estrutura do fruto parece um olho.

Segundo a equipe da miss, a produção do traje exigiu um mês de trabalho e mobilizou mais de 25 profissionais, entre artesãos, bordadeiras, especialistas em tecidos plissados e impressão 3D.

Somente no Atelier Bruno Oliveira, uma equipe de 15 pessoas trabalhou diretamente na confecção da peça, que recebeu mais de 80 metros de tecidos plissados.

Marcella, que é natural de Curitiba (PR), participou diretamente do processo criativo.

'Quem vai querer saber da minha história?': A foto que mostrou ao mundo a luta por moradia digna no Brasil

Pessoa presa em tirolesa, banheiros químicos arrastados e secretário ferido: Temporal causa estragos no Paraná

Conforme a equipe da miss, o objetivo do traje é despertar a curiosidade do público internacional sobre o fruto, chamar a atenção para a biodiversidade brasileira e enviar uma mensagem sobre valorização da natureza e sustentabilidade.

Em vermelho, o traje combina volumes, texturas e brilho para formar uma estrutura que remete à natureza. Uma iluminação em LED ajuda a valorizar os detalhes do figurino.

Folhas produzidas com garrafas PET verdes recicladas adornam o traje. Elas foram pintadas e ornamentadas com cristais.

Já os detalhes que representam os frutos de guaraná ganharam forma por meio da impressão 3D.

Desfile dos trajes típicos apresenta ao mundo cultura dos países

No desfile dos trajes típicos, cada candidata usa um figurino para representar a cultura, a história, a biodiversidade ou a fé do país.

Para Rodrigo Ferro, da direção do Miss Universe Brasil, a escolha do traje nacional vai muito além da estética e reforça a importância de utilizar a visibilidade de uma competição internacional para apresentar ao mundo as riquezas do país.

"Quando o Brasil chega a um palco como o do Miss Universo, temos a oportunidade de mostrar ao mundo muito mais do que beleza. Cada traje que apresentamos carrega um propósito. Queremos valorizar a nossa cultura, chamar a atenção para as riquezas naturais do país e despertar a curiosidade das pessoas. Não se trata de criar um figurino apenas para impressionar. Queremos que ele também informe, represente e deixe uma mensagem. É uma oportunidade de mostrar ao mundo a grandeza do Brasil", destaca Rodrigo Ferro.

A proposta se reflete nas escolhas feitas pelas candidatas, que costumam recorrer a símbolos religiosos, elementos da fauna, personagens históricos e referências culturais para representar seus países.

Em 2025, por exemplo, a candidata Gabriela Lacerda, que representava o Brasil no concurso, usou um vestido inspirado em Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

Naquele mesmo ano, a norueguesa Leonora Lysglimt-Rødland viralizou ao desfilar com uma fantasia inusitada que remetia a um salmão. A candidata Audrey Eckert, que representava os Estados Unidos, usou um traje inspirado na águia-de-cabeça-branca. Brigitta Schaback, representante da Estônia, usou uma fantasia inspirada em um lobo e na obra literária estoniana Libahunt (Lobisomem).

Representante do Brasil, dos EUA, da Noruega e da Estônia durante o desfile de trajes típicos no Miss Universo 2025 — Foto: AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit | REUTERS/Athit Perawongmetha | REUTERS/Athit

O desfile de traje típico ocorre às 20h deste sábado. No domingo (22), ocorrem, no mesmo horário, os desfiles em traje de banho e vestido de gala, além de entrevista com os jurados.

Na terça-feira (24), às 22h, ocorre a grande final.

articles.title: Ícaro, da dupla com Gilmar, anuncia pausa em shows  | G1
articles.standfirst: Em vídeo divulgado nas redes sociais, o cantor foi diagnosticado com síndrome compartimental na perna direita, precisou imobilizar a perna. Ele recebeu recomendação de repouso absoluto.
articles.summary: Cantor foi diagnosticado com síndrome compartimental na perna direita, precisou imobilizar o membro e cumpre repouso absoluto para evitar cirurgia.
articles.body:
O cantor sertanejo Ícaro, da dupla com Gilmar, anunciou nas redes sociais que vai se afastar temporariamente dos palcos após receber o diagnóstico de síndrome compartimental na perna direita. Ele disse que começou a sentir fortes dores no início da semana e, após passar por exames médicos, recebeu recomendação de repouso absoluto com a perna elevada (assista acima) .

Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, Ícaro relatou estar sob uso de medicamentos fortes e pediu orações pela sua recuperação. No vídeo, o cantor avisa que não poderá comparecer nos próximos shows e pede para que os fãs não fiquem chateados.

"Estou bem assustado. Não quero que aconteça o pior. Sou um cara que sempre luto para entregar o melhor, mas hoje não vai rolar. Peço que vocês orem por mim. Para que melhorar logo isso daqui, que não precisa ir para o próximo passo, que é a cirurgia. E que vocês cantem hoje lá, junto com eles", disse.

O cantor, que passou por uma cirurgia em julho após sofrer uma lesão na mão direita ao fim de um show , explicou que precisa ficar com a perna elevada para tentar conter a inflamação muscular e evitar a necessidade de uma cirurgia de descompressão (fasciotomia) .

Sertanejo Ícaro, da dupla com Gilmar, anuncia pausa em shows após descobrir inflamação na perna: 'Tô bem assustado' — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram Ícaro e Gilmar

Henrique e Juliano lamentam 'profundamente' a ausência em shows após cirurgia: 'Valores recebidos serão integralmente ressarcidos'

Os médicos advertiram sobre a gravidade da lesão, segundo o artista, pontuando que o comprometimento da circulação sanguínea e a perda de mobilidade do membro tornavam o repouso imediato inegociável.

Diante do quadro, o músico relatou que precisou ser medicado com morfina para suportar a dor. Ele explicou ainda que, caso o repouso com elevação da perna não reverta a compressão muscular, a fasciotomia exigirá que a perna permaneça com a incisão aberta de 7 a 15 dias no hospital para restabelecer o fluxo sanguíneo.

Mesmo afastado, Ícaro garantiu que acompanhará os shows da equipe e do parceiro diretamente de casa durante sua recuperação.

articles.title: SP-127 em Tatuí terá desvios no trânsito até 2027; veja mudanças | G1
articles.standfirst: As mudanças no km 113+570 devem durar até o 2º semestre de 2027. Durante o período, os motoristas usarão os acostamentos.
articles.summary: A concessionária SPVias inicia obras de remodelação no km 113 da SP-127 em Tatuí, desviando o tráfego para os acostamentos em três alças de acesso até o ano de 2027.
articles.body:
Obras em trevo provocam mudanças no trânsito da SP-127 em Tatuí a partir desta segunda-feira (23) — Foto: SPVias/Divulgação

A concessionária SPVias inicia nesta segunda-feira (23) um desvio temporário de tráfego em três alças de retorno no km 113+570 da Rodovia Antônio Romano Schincariol (SP-127), em Tatuí (SP).

As mudanças devem permanecer até o segundo semestre de 2027. Durante esse período, os motoristas serão direcionados para os acostamentos, que estarão sinalizados para garantir a circulação pelo trecho.

A alteração faz parte das obras de remodelação do trevo, que têm como objetivo aumentar a segurança viária e melhorar a fluidez do trânsito na região.

Entrada para Tatuí: acesso pela SP-127 Norte, no sentido Cerquilho–Tatuí;

Acesso à SP-127 Norte: saída da SP-141 em direção a Cerquilho;

Acesso à SP-127 Sul: saída da SP-141 em direção a Itapetininga.

Segundo a concessionária, os acessos continuarão disponíveis durante as obras, mas os motoristas deverão utilizar os desvios sinalizados nos acostamentos.

A SPVias recomenda que os motoristas reduzam a velocidade ao se aproximarem do trecho, respeitem a sinalização provisória, mantenham distância segura do veículo à frente e evitem mudanças bruscas de faixa.

A concessionária também orienta que os deslocamentos sejam planejados com antecedência e que os condutores sigam as instruções das equipes operacionais.

Em caso de dúvidas ou necessidade de atendimento, os motoristas podem entrar em contato com a concessionária pelo telefone 0800 703 5030, que também atende pelo WhatsApp.

articles.title: Bell Marques em Maceió: JHC confirma show para 1º de janeiro de 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Governador eleito confirmou a apresentação nas redes sociais e chamou os fãs do cantor de “bellzeiros”; música que leva o nome do público viralizou na internet em novembro.
articles.summary: Bell Marques em Maceió terá show confirmado pelo governador eleito JHC para o dia 1º de janeiro de 2027, celebrando o sucesso da música viral "Sou Bellzeiro".
articles.body:
Arrastão do Bell Marques em Maceió — Foto: Reprodução/Secom Maceió

O cantor Bell Marques fará show na orla de Maceió no dia 1º de janeiro de 2027. O anúncio da apresentação foi feito pelo governador eleito de Alagoas, JHC (PSDB), na sexta-feira (20), pelas redes sociais.

Em 2026, o já artista se apresentou na cidade em diferentes ocasiões, incluindo o tradicional arrastão do dia 1º de janeiro e no São João da capital.

Na publicação, JHC declarou ser fã do cantor e convocou o público para acompanhar a apresentação.

“Somos Bellzeiros, campeão! A orla de Maceió dia 1º vai representar! Todos os Bellzeiros vão rodar o Brasil pra estar aqui!”, escreveu o governador eleito, acompanhado de emojis de comemoração, sol e mar.

A referência feita por JHC aos “bellzeiros” está relacionada à música “Sou Bellzeiro”, lançada recentemente por Bell Marques em homenagem à sua trajetória e à relação com os fãs.

A canção foi composta por Filipe Escandurras, Shylton Fernandes e Samir Trindade. A música ganhou repercussão nas redes sociais no início de novembro de 2026 e passou a integrar o repertório dos shows do cantor.

A gravação oficial em estúdio aconteceu depois da estreia ao vivo. A iniciativa também contou com o incentivo de Pipo Marques, filho do artista, que fez campanha nas redes sociais para que o pai registrasse a faixa.

Na letra, Bell Marques celebra a relação com os fãs, incluindo referências aos chamados “bellzeiros do Velho Testamento”.

articles.title: Paulo do Peixe: morre fundador de restaurante em Volta Redonda | G1
articles.standfirst: Velório será realizado neste sábado (21), a partir das 19h, na capela 3 do Portal da Saudade. Sepultamento está marcado para domingo (22).
articles.summary: Paulo do Peixe, fundador do tradicional restaurante em Volta Redonda, faleceu aos 79 anos; o velório ocorre neste sábado (21) no cemitério Portal da Saudade.
articles.body:
Morre Paulo do Peixe, fundador de restaurante, aos 79 anos, em Volta Redonda — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O empresário Paulo Peres, conhecido como 'Paulo do Peixe', fundador do Restaurante Paulo do Peixe, morreu. O falecimento foi comunicado neste sábado (21), por meio de uma nota publicada nas redes sociais.

Na publicação, Paulo foi lembrado como um homem empreendedor, apaixonado pela vida e pela família, que marcou gerações com seu carinho, alegria e jeito único de receber as pessoas.

"É com profundo pesar que comunicamos o falecimento de Paulo, fundador do Restaurante Paulo do Peixe, um homem de bem, empreendedor, apaixonado pela vida e por sua família", diz um trecho da nota do restaurante.

O corpo será levado para o Portal da Saudade, onde o velório será realizado a partir das 19h deste sábado, na capela 3. O sepultamento está marcado para domingo (22), às 11h.

Em razão do falecimento, o Restaurante Paulo do Peixe informou que não funcionará neste domingo.

articles.title: Parada LGBT+ de Jundiapeba: confira a programação  | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento tem concentração a partir das 12h, na estação de Jundiapeba, e segue até o Largo da Feira. Organização espera reunir entre 1 mil e 1,5 mil pessoas.
articles.summary: A Parada LGBT+ de Jundiapeba terá concentração na estação às 12h e caminhada até o Largo da Feira com shows de Gael Vicci e diversos artistas do Alto Tietê.
articles.body:
1ª edição da Parada LGBT+ de Jundiapeba acontece neste domingo — Foto: Sophie Emeny/Unsplash

A 1ª edição da Parada LGBT+ de Jundiapeba acontece neste domingo (22), em Mogi das Cruzes . A concentração está marcada para as 12h, em frente à estação de trem do distrito. Depois, os participantes seguem em caminhada até o Largo da Feira.

🏳‍🌈 A organização estima reunir entre 1 mil e 1,5 mil pessoas. O evento conta com apresentações de artistas locais e do Alto Tietê, além de convidados. A programação também inclui apresentações de cantores e atrações ligadas à cultura LGBT+.

O presidente da Parada LGBT+ de Jundiapeba, Edrei Freitas, explicou que a iniciativa busca ampliar a visibilidade da comunidade nos bairros mais afastados do centro da cidade.

"Nem todas as pessoas têm a possibilidade ou a facilidade de ir até o centro de Mogi das Cruzes. Com as paradas periféricas, levamos visibilidade das pessoas LGBT+ para os bairros", afirmou.

O tema escolhido para esta primeira edição é "Nossa Existência é Resistência: a Periferia também é Orgulho!" . Segundo Edrei, a proposta também é valorizar a cultura da comunidade e dar espaço a artistas da periferia.

Gael Vicci e Diego Rivera se apresentam na Parada LGBT+ de Jundiapeba — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A apresentação ficará por conta de Tiffany Brandão e Antonieta Salt. Entre os convidados está Gael Vicci, que participou do reality musical Estrelas da Casa, da TV Globo , além do rapper Diego Rivera. Também estão previstas apresentações de artistas moradores de Jundiapeba e de outras cidades do Alto Tietê (confira abaixo).

Edrei também é diretor da Parada LGBT+ de Mogi das Cruzes, que chegou à oitava edição neste ano. Ele destacou que a realização de um evento desse porte em Jundiapeba representa um marco para a descentralização das atividades voltadas à comunidade LGBT+ na cidade.

A Parada é organizada pela Associação Casa da Diversidade em Ação, entidade LGBTQIAPN+ da qual Edrei é presidente. De acordo com ele, até o momento, a organização não conseguiu parceiros para oferecer serviços à população.

O evento conta com duas tendas parceiras, uma de espetinhos e outra de bebidas.

Local de concentração : Estação de Jundiapeba

Trajeto : caminhada até o Largo da Feira

Público estimado : de 1 mil a 1,5 mil pessoas

Organização : Associação Casa da Diversidade em Ação

articles.title: Cantores sertanejos mudam planos após fortes temporais no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: César Menotti & Fabiano e Israel & Rodolffo tiveram que cancelar voos, e Felipe Araújo encerrou show antecipadamente devido à força dos ventos e da chuva.
articles.summary: César Menotti & Fabiano e Israel & Rodolffo tiveram que cancelar voos, e Felipe Araújo encerrou show antecipadamente devido à força dos ventos e da chuva.
articles.body:
As duplas sertanejas César Menotti & Fabiano e Israel & Rodolffo, que estavam no Paraná para agenda de shows, tiveram que cancelar voos devido às condições climáticas no estado, nesta sexta-feira (20).

Ainda, o cantor Felipe Araújo encerrou um evento antes do previsto devido à força dos ventos que, segundo ele, começaram a balançar a estrutura do palco. Veja os detalhes abaixo.

César Menotti e Fabiano não conseguem pousar em Foz do Iguaçu

César Menotti, da dupla com Fabiano Menotti, publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais contando que eles saíram de Belo Horizonte, em Minas Gerais, de avião, com destino a Foz do Iguaçu. No entanto, devido aos temporais, a aeronave em que estavam não pôde pousar na cidade e o voo precisou ser desviado para Cascavel , cidade a cerca de 140 quilômetros do destino inicial.

Os artistas viajaram para o Paraná para uma apresentação no Leilão Cataratas, evento privado do agronegócio marcado para este sábado (21), em Foz do Iguaçu.

"Pousamos agora em Cascavel . Esse tempo está difícil para quem viaja", disse César Menotti em vídeo.

César Menotti & Fabiano, Israel & Rodolffo e Felipe Araújo relataram mudanças de planos — Foto: Fotos: Redes Sociais

Neste sábado (21), o cantor fez outra postagem afirmando que a dupla optou por seguir de carro de Cascavel para Foz do Iguaçu: "Vamos de carro que carro é mais conveniente neste momento", explicou.

Israel & Rodolffo desistem de viajar de avião saindo de Pato Branco

Durante a tarde, em Pato Branco, no Sudoeste do Paraná, Rodolffo Matthaus da Silva Rios, da dupla com Israel Antônio Ribeiro, postou um vídeo nas redes sociais contando que a dupla desistiu de partir em uma viagem de avião devido aos temporais que atingiram a cidade.

Na quinta-feira (19), a dupla fez uma apresentação em São Jorge do Oeste, cidade vizinha, e partiria para Balneário Camboriú (SC), onde se apresentam no sábado (21). "Chegamos a entrar dentro do avião para decolar", relatou Rodolffo, em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais.

Segundo o cantor, a desistência aconteceu depois que outro avião pousou no aeroporto e informou que as condições não estavam favoráveis.

"Tem que respeitar o clima, tem que respeitar o tempo. Não iremos mais hoje. Mas, graças a Deus, está tudo certo. Nós não temos compromisso hoje", afirmou.

O cantor compartilhou nas redes que saiu para jantar em Pato Branco e, neste sábado (21), seguiu avião de avião e chegou em segurança em Balneário Camboriú (SC): "Hoje deu bão", comentou.

Felipe Araújo encerra show antecipadamente em Cambé devido a vendaval

O cantor Felipe Araújo encerrou antes do previsto o show que fazia em Cambé, no Norte do Paraná , na noite de sexta-feira (20), devido a força dos ventos.

Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, o cantor contou que o tempo mudou rapidamente durante a apresentação. Segundo ele, fazia cerca de 30°C e, de repente, os ventos ficaram tão fortes que começaram a balançar a estrutura do palco.

"O vento estava me empurrando ali em cima do palco. Aí eu resolvi parar o show porque fiquei preocupado com os equipamentos que estavam balançando muito", relatou.

O cantor ainda relatou que não se sentiu seguro nem mesmo no camarim e que buscou abrigo em um veículo. "Agora eu tô aqui na van, pelo menos aqui onde eu tô tá seguro. Mas até ali no palco, ali no camarim, estava tudo balançando demais e estava muito, muito, muito, muito perigoso", disse.

Temporais no Paraná causaram queda de estruturas e de árvores

O Paraná foi atingido por fortes tempestades, especialmente nas regiões Sudoeste, Oeste, Norte e Noroeste. Em Foz do Iguaçu, por exemplo, casas ficaram destelhadas e houve o registro de nuvens em formato de funil . Em Cascavel, uma estrutura cedeu no Autódromo Internacional Zilmar Beux, pouco antes do previsto para a prova de automobilismo 40ª Cascavel de Ouro.

Em Maringá , uma árvore de decoração natalina de 20 metros caiu e uma pessoa ficou presa em uma tirolesa . articles.title: Hat eaten by Fiona the hippo lodged deep in small intestine, necropsy shows
articles.summary: Fans expressed their love for the famous Nile hippopotamus at Cincinnati Zoo after it died aged nine.
articles.body:
A necropsy on Fiona, the popular hippo at Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden in the United States, showed that the hat she swallowed was lodged deep inside her body and veterinary staff were unable to reach it before she died.

The hat was “25 feet [7.60 metres] beyond the final stomach compartment and 50 feet [15.2 metres] from the end of her intestines,” said a statement released on Friday by the zoo in Ohio.

Fiona was nine years old when she died. Hippos typically live 40 to 50 years in zoos. The hat she ingested had accidentally been flung into her enclosure.

Since her death, fans have covered the zoo with flowers and notes, while others left behind her favourite treats, including melons and pumpkins.

“We have received so much love from our community and beyond,” said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike.

The Nile hippopotamus was born prematurely in January 2017. Weighing just 29 pounds (13.2 kg), far below the lowest recorded birth weight for her species, she became a source of pride and a symbol of hope locally and nationwide.

Fiona inspired millions in her first months and final days, bringing people together across political divides and other boundaries.

Usha Vance, wife of Vice President JD Vance, posted a photo on Instagram of one of their children face-to-face with Fiona.

Former first daughter Chelsea Clinton posted photos of her behind-the-scenes encounter with Fiona, writing that she would treasure “the smiles she gave me”.

Jenna Wingate, one of Fiona’s keepers, posted a message on Instagram, remembering the creature that brought joy to many around the world.

“It has always felt like we grew up together, and I often used to smile thinking about growing old with her and her still being around when I retire,” Wingate wrote. “We lost her in the most horrific and tragic way.”

“She was our family. I love you Fiona and I am so sorry.”

Fiona’s digestive system could not handle the hat’s synthetic fibres, experts told The Associated Press news agency.

Blood analysis showed that her health was failing on Thursday, so the zoo’s animal care team tried to locate the hat using a scope and an ultrasound, said Mike Wenninger, the zoo’s director of animal health. Removing the hat surgically was impossible based on its location and the hippo’s anatomy, he added.

Fiona died during recovery from the procedure, he said.

“Keepers, vets, staff and volunteers are shaken and trying to navigate this loss,” said the Cincinnati Zoo in a statement. “She meant a lot to a lot of people.”

As for Fiona’s fellow hippos, Bibi, Tucker and Fritz, they appear to be behaving normally, said Christina Gorsuch, Cincinnati Zoo’s director of animal care.

“It’s difficult to know how they’re feeling, but they appear to be their normal selves,” she said.

articles.title: Inside Georgia woman’s Emmanuel’s Village: 15 tiny homes on vacant land behind her business, giving homeless families a safe place to live. Meet Molly Holm and her initiative turning unused property into housing and a fresh start for families in need
articles.summary: A pickle jar, an eight-year-old boy, and a man sleeping in his car.
articles.body: A pickle jar, an eight-year-old boy, and a man sleeping in his car. It sounds like the start of a children’s book, but it is the real beginning of Emmanuel’s Village in Marietta, Georgia, a planned community of 15 tiny homes for families who have nowhere stable to go.A boy who noticedMolly Holm owns Glory Haus, a business with a warehouse in Marietta. Her son Luke, then 8, noticed that one of the employees there was living out of his car. Plenty of people might have looked away. Luke started a fundraiser instead, “Pickles with a Purpose,” selling homemade pickles. The money was enough to put a roof over that employee’s head for four years.Writer Maya Angelou is often credited with saying that people will forget what you said, but never how you made them feel. A kid with a jar of pickles seems to have understood that without being told.From one person to hundredsFour years of housing for one man proved something to Holm: small efforts can work. But the need around her was far bigger. More than 500 students in the Marietta City School District experience homelessness. Behind her warehouse sat 1.4 acres of unused land. Holm teamed up with local nonprofits, churches and groups like MUST Ministries to turn that empty patch into something permanent.What the village looks likeEach of the 15 homes will measure between 24 and 32 feet long. Inside are two lofted bedrooms, a full bathroom, a galley kitchen, a living area, heating and air conditioning, a washer and dryer, and internet access. That last item matters more than it sounds, since a child with no internet at home has a hard time keeping up with school.Beyond the houses, the plan includes a playground, community gardens and a community center. The center will be a repurposed Fort Wilderness cabin from Disney World, a quirky detail that gives the place some personality.A bridge, not a destinationEmmanuel’s Village is built to be temporary. Approved by the Marietta City Council, it lets families stay between six months and two years while receiving wrap-around support services aimed at building financial stability and moving into permanent housing.Critics of tiny-home projects often point out that they treat symptoms, not causes. Fair enough. But a stable address is often what makes a job search, a school routine or a doctor’s visit possible. Here, the support services are what separate a shelter from a stepping stone.The money questionThe project is expected to cost about $3 million to $3.2 million. Roughly half has been raised through private donations and community sponsorships. To cover the rest, Holm and her partners have pursued state grant opportunities, including Georgia’s Rehouse Georgia initiative.Half funded is encouraging, though not finished. The gap is real, and the village will need steady backing to open its doors. Still, it began with pickles, so small beginnings seem to suit this story.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly reported information and is for general informational purposes only. articles.title: Crew evacuated amid battle to put out fire on Russian ship hit by drones
articles.summary: Finnish authorities say two drones attack cargo ship that has links to Russia’s armed forces.
articles.body:
The crew of a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland, hit by drones likely launched by Ukraine, has now been evacuated to a nearby cargo ship and will reportedly be taken directly back to Russia.

Finnish authorities say the Sparta II has links to Russia’s armed forces and is currently anchored off the southern Finnish town of Loviisa, where firefighting efforts are still ongoing at sea.

Operations at the scene, involving extinguishing the fire on board the Sparta II and cooling the vessel, are being carried out by rescue units and patrol ships from the Finnish Border Guard, a patrol aircraft and helicopters. Two Finnish civilian rescue tugs are also involved, as well as an Estonian navy patrol ship.

“At the request of the Border Guard, the Russian rescue ship Murman is also participating in the rescue operations,” Finnish authorities said in a statement.

Finnish Defence Minister Antti Hakkanen told the Helsingin Sanomat newspaper that the Sparta II would be towed out of Finland’s territorial waters on Saturday night.

On Saturday morning, Finland’s Ministry of Defence said its forces detected a drone attack on a Russian vessel in international waters, with initial reports saying the ship had sustained damage. Finnish Border Guard units were dispatched to the scene, and a photograph taken by a Finnish patrol plane showed flames and thick smoke coming from the rear of the ship.

The attack happened west of Gogland Island, off the coast of the Finnish town of Loviisa, and Finland quickly implemented temporary air and sea traffic restrictions in the eastern part of the gulf.

A Russian helicopter has since violated Finnish airspace, venturing more than 4km (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.

“The suspected airspace violation is possibly related to rescue or tracking operations of a damaged cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. The Defence Forces and the Border Guard are handling the situation in cooperation with other authorities,” said Hakkanen.

By Saturday afternoon, the Finnish Defence Forces said the strike was likely carried out by Ukraine. Earlier, Finland’s Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote on X that “war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity. The Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor”.

Finland’s Border Guard said the Sparta II is known to have links to Russia’s armed forces. The roll-on/roll-off ship was built in the year 2000 and sails under a Russian flag, according to the VesselFinder website.

“At the moment, ⁠⁠⁠⁠there is no confirmed information about ⁠⁠⁠⁠what cargo is on ⁠⁠⁠⁠board, but ⁠⁠⁠⁠it cannot be ruled out that there ‌‌‌‌is military materiel on board,” said Commander Ilja Iljin from the Finnish Border Guard.

The governor of Russia’s Leningrad region, Alexander Drozdenko, said earlier on Saturday that damage to the ship had yet to be fully assessed.

“Three nautical miles [5.6km] from the Russian Federation’s border, a cargo vessel bound for Kaliningrad was attacked by two drones,” he wrote on the messaging app Max, shortly after the attack.

Kaliningrad’s Governor Alexey Besprozvannykh said supplies to the Russian exclave were not at risk.

One of the major risks of attacking any vessel is environmental damage if it leaks or sinks, a scenario that Baltic Sea nations treat with high importance. That risk is “further amplified by the poor state of some of the so-called ‘Shadow Fleet’ tankers” that Russia operates, according to Robin Haggblom, senior adviser for Risk Intelligence and an expert in Finnish maritime issues.

“Actions to prevent environmental damage has also been emphasised in Finnish Border Guard communication regarding this event. Luckily in this case, we don’t yet have ice coverage in the Gulf of Finland, which would impact any oil spill recovery efforts that may be needed,” Haggblom told Al Jazeera.

The narrow and shallow waters of the Baltic Sea are some of the most crowded shipping lanes in the world. The Helsinki to Tallinn ferry route had 7.5 million passenger crossings last year. Other passenger routes link Baltic ports and capital cities, and cargo vessels and military shipping contribute to the total number of vessels in the relatively small body of water.

So if Ukraine is using drones – maritime or aerial – to hit Russian ships, there could be risks to civilian vessels.

“There obviously always is a risk of collateral damage. However, so far Ukraine does seem to be taking a number of steps to minimise the risks involved, with the Sparta II, for example, apparently having been identified and hit a handful of kilometres from Russian waters,” added Haggblom.

Earlier this month, Finland’s military said it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, which Ukraine took credit for. Helsinki later said it had raised concerns with Kyiv about strikes in the area.

“It is the same with the strike on the Russian corvette earlier, where it is reported the Ukrainians were able to pick it out and target that specific vessel among perhaps a dozen other ships. There are also unconfirmed indications that Sparta II was targeted specifically, and not just as a general Russia-associated merchant vessel,” Haggblom added.

Ukraine and Russia have attacked each other’s shipping throughout the war, mostly in the Black Sea.

articles.title: An Indian-origin hotelier in New York forced staff to work 112 hours a week without pay, threatened them with deportation, told them he had close ties to the 'head of immigration'
articles.summary: Dozens of immigrant workers renovating a former Holiday Inn in Rochester, New York, were allegedly forced to work as many as 112 hours a week, went months
articles.body: Dozens of immigrant workers renovating a former Holiday Inn in Rochester, New York, were allegedly forced to work as many as 112 hours a week, went months without receiving wages and were threatened with deportation when they demanded payment, according to a lawsuit filed by New York Attorney General Letitia James. The civil lawsuit, filed on November 19, names InterContinental Hotels Group (IHG), the former hotel's owner Nayan Patel and renovation contractor Roman Petrik among the defendants. It accuses them of benefiting from an alleged forced-labour scheme involving dozens of immigrant workers recruited from different states and countries.According to the complaint, workers were promised hourly wages and accommodation at the hotel in exchange for renovating the property. However, they allegedly received little or no payment for months while continuing to work long hours. Some workers reportedly went at least eight months without being paid. The lawsuit alleged that workers who questioned the missing wages were threatened with eviction, arrest and deportation. The complaint also claims that the contractor told workers he could have them deported whenever he wanted. He told them he had close ties to the 'head of immigration'The workers were reportedly recruited to renovate different sections of the hotel as part of a project that began in 2023.Workers allegedly housed in pest-infested rooms with no electricity or running waterThe lawsuit further alleges that workers and their families, including children, were made to live on the hotel's abandoned seventh floor from September 2023 to make room for paying guests. The floor, which had reportedly been out of service since at least 2016, lacked basic facilities, including electricity, running water, functioning toilets and showers, and heating and cooling systems.The rooms allegedly had no working door locks and were infested with pests and vermin. Workers and their children were forced to spend the winter in the unheated rooms, with some reportedly falling ill because of the living conditions and exposure to construction dust, paint and extreme cold.One worker was promised $18 an hour and worked approximately 68 hours a week for 29 weeks. He should have received around $30,506 but was allegedly paid only $2,200 during that period.Contractor accused of sexually assaulting workerThe lawsuit contains another serious allegation against contractor Roman Petrik. He is accused of repeatedly sexually assaulting a female worker and threatening to withhold her wages if she did not comply.The complaint alleges that workers who demanded their outstanding wages faced intimidation and retaliation. At least three workers were allegedly evicted after seeking payment.Lawsuit alleges Holiday Inn parent company knew about workers' plightThe lawsuit also raises questions about what IHG, the parent company of Holiday Inn, knew about the alleged exploitation. According to the complaint, IHG officials visited the hotel on June 14, 2024, inspected the seventh floor and spoke with workers who told them they had not been paid for at least eight months and were living in unacceptable conditions.Four days later, an IHG regional executive allegedly emailed Patel, describing the people living on the seventh floor as squatters and asking him to remove them because they posed security and reputational risks to the Holiday Inn brand. New York's attorney general alleges that IHG failed to investigate the workers' complaints or report the suspected exploitation despite being made aware of their circumstances.IHG, however, denied knowing about the alleged misconduct."We emphatically deny that IHG had any knowledge of serious misconduct by the hotel owner or contractor as alleged in the lawsuit," the company said in a statement, adding that it strongly condemns human trafficking and believes the hotel owner and contractor should be held responsible for any violations of the law.What happened to the Rochester hotel?The property, which was previously operated as a Holiday Inn in downtown Rochester, was rebranded as a Wyndham in January 2025. Rochester authorities ordered it closed in June 2026 over fire safety and other building code violations. The hotel had also housed asylum seekers arriving from New York City in 2023, a period that overlapped with the alleged exploitation of renovation workers.You use AI every day. articles.title: Scouts say they face £1m tourist tax cost for overnight trips
articles.summary: The increased cost after the proposed Visitors Levy is imposed could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said.
articles.body:
Scout groups are warning they could face an additional annual bill of £1m as a result of the government's proposed tourist tax for England.

The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services.

The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said.

Dwayne Fields, the UK's Chief Scout, has called for youth groups to be exempted and said the charity - which sees more than 1.4m overnight stays a year - would be "firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations".

The Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government told the BBC that local leaders who introduce the levy "will have the option to exempt certain types of accommodation in their areas, including accommodation which is often used for trips by youth groups like Scouts and Girl Guides - such as camping pitches".

They added money raised from the levy will "stay local and be invested in the visitor experience and local growth including in high streets, parks and events".

Labour mayors have indicated they would cap the levy at 5% but the legislation contains no maximum limit.

In a statement, the Scout Association said the tax, if set at 5% across the country, could cost the charity £1.04m a year and force volunteers to deal with onerous paperwork.

They worked this out by assuming the levy would be set at 5% for all the 1,423,344 annual overnight stays across Squirrels, Beavers, Cubs, Scouts, Explorers and volunteers.

Girlguiding would also be subject to the levy.

In a statement, Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity.

"But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

Chris Taylor, lead volunteer for Greater Manchester East Scout County, called the levy a "tent tax" and branded it "madness".

Referring to the levy being applied to the Linnet Clough campsite run by his group in Stockport, he said: "Our members spent nearly 25,000 nights away from home last year, and a 5% levy would add over £11,000 a year to the cost of their camps and sleepovers."

He added: "On top of that, and as a charity, we'd have to employ someone just to collect the tax and send returns to the Mayor's office. That's another £7,000 a year, and that's just one campsite - there are plenty more across Manchester."

Labour MP Gareth Snell, who challenged ministers when the levy was debated in the House of Commons , said Scouts "provide some of the most memorable experiences for young people up and down the country."

The Stoke-on-Trent Central MP called on the government to take the decision out of mayors' hands and ensure Scout camps are exempted from the bill.

The Welsh Government has announced young people staying in hostels, campsites or outdoor centres would be exempt from its tourism tax, due to come into effect next year.

articles.title: Tech outages give broadcast media just another opportunity to bash Republicans
articles.summary: America faced a week of tech woes as banks, Microsoft email and Apple Pay failed after the ground stop, and Whoopi Goldberg blamed Elon Musk's DOGE.
articles.body: Whenever anything goes wrong in America, the broadcast networks have a reflex to suggest things must have gone awry because the Trump administration is so remarkably incompetent and unqualified to govern anything. It began last weekend when a nationwide ground stop underlined a problem with the nation’s air traffic control system, which still used floppy disks. On the Sunday shows, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy received the same antagonistic routine from the broadcast hosts: Why haven’t you done anything about this? At every stop, Duffy explained that the Trump administration has been trying to get funding for a revamp, but Congress was very specific in how it appropriated funds. Duffy had an answer, but Trump had to be blamed. Don’t try suggesting that the Obama and Biden administrations passed massive infrastructure bills and somehow didn’t get this job done. The New York Post reported Biden’s Transportation Department under Secretary Pete Buttigieg spent $80 billion on DEI programs. The networks weren’t going to be outraged or offended at the contrast. DUFFY VOWS TO MODERNIZE AGING AIR TRAFFIC SYSTEM AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP On the left-wing late-night comedy shows, the networks made fun of Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin as unqualified. On NBC’s "Tonight Show," Jimmy Fallon interviewed Duffy and Mullin impersonators. "I'm not sure you guys are inspiring a lot of confidence from the American people." Fake Duffy replied, "Look, I'm a former ‘Real World’-‘Road Rules’ reality TV contestant who's wearing this stupid little jacket like I'm Airplane Ken." Fake Mullin added, "And I'm a former UFC fighter who's been hit in the head so many times, my brain issued a nationwide ground stop for my thoughts." DHS CHIEF TELLS AMERICANS TO 'BREATHE' AMID TECH OUTAGES, INSISTS HOMELAND IS 'SECURE' ABC’s Jimmy Kimmel – who sampled two different colleges for one year after high school and never returned or graduated – pulled the same routine. "We learned, this weekend, a very valuable lesson. We learned what happens when the only experience your secretary of Transportation has when it comes to transportation is being on ‘Road Rules: All Stars’ on MTV." Later, he added: "Fortunately, they have got some of the top minds working on this, like plumber-turned head of Homeland Security, the router-rooter Markwayne Mullin." They pretend these men didn’t serve in the House and Senate, like they were plucked off the street. The tech incidents piled up during the week. Several banks had problems. Many Microsoft users were locked out of their email systems, crippling their offices. Apple users said Tuesday morning they were unable to use the App Store, Apple Pay and other services. At the National Security Agency outside Washington, an internal communications network went down. The agency announced this happened during scheduled routine maintenance. MICROSOFT’S MASSIVE OUTAGE OFFERS A LESSON IN HOW TO BRING THE WORLD BACK ONLINE All of these things made Americans wonder about what could go wrong. Then people start talking about stocking up on food and water and generators like some catastrophe is in the offing. Speaking of unqualified comedians, Whoopi Goldberg came on "The View" with more of her crackpot conspiracy theories. All this was happening right after the Democrats won big. "I just find it interesting that all of these things that have been put in place, suddenly, suddenly now, two weeks after a blue wave, everything's going wrong. Everything is kind of weird. Call me paranoid." She blamed Elon Musk: "But the man in charge of DOGE has a lot of stuff in the air and he seems to have control over a lot of things that go on around the world. It just - It makes me uncomfortable." She repeated her blue-wave conspiracies as the week went on. MAMDANI TAKES SWIPE AT TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S RESPONSE TO TECH OUTAGES: 'FAR FROM WHAT MANY WANTED TO HEAR' Kimmel even made fun of the argument that the temporary ground stop wasn’t deadly. He played a clip of Texas Republican Rep. Michael McCaul at a hearing telling Mullin: "I'm going to start with you, Mr. Secretary. First of all, let me commend you, 36,000 planes being grounded. Yes, it was chaotic. But you know what, nobody died." Kimmel reacted by laughing as if McCaul was giving Mullin credit for clearing the lowest of low bars, "Nobody died? Of course nobody died. None of the planes were able to take off." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION This marks the way "holding the government accountable" works at the networks. When something goes wrong with a Democrat president in power, the journalistic assumption is that you can’t blame the Democrats. Things just happened. Let’s not connect any dots. It’s the absolute opposite with Republicans. You can connect dots that don’t make a straight line. Democrats are presumed to be competent and well-educated. But part of that confidence mission is based on network TV stars badgering them as The Problem. This partisan media system is especially frustrating when people are honestly scared. articles.title: Aldi apologises over parking cherry picker at vets in Matlock
articles.summary: Derwent Valley Vets named the cherry picker a "Specialbuy" after it was left in the car park.
articles.body:
A good-natured dispute between a major supermarket and a veterinary practice has ended after some jokey posts on social media.

Derwent Valley Vets, in Matlock in Derbyshire, posted that a cherry picker linked to the building of a new Aldi nearby was taking up spaces in its small car park after it appeared on Wednesday.

Named "Shiny Blue Lifty McLiftface", the vets teasingly said: "If the cherry picker is going to be this week's Specialbuy, please let us know" - but then joked about being "ghosted" by the retailer.

By Friday, Aldi responded with an apology and the offer to "donate a woofing big hamper of pet food to a local shelter of your choice. Just tell them Santa Paws has come early".

Claire Goodear, co-owner of the business, explained Aldi had previously kept them informed of potential disruption during building work.

But on Wednesday the machine appeared in their car park and, despite appeals, stayed put.

She said the cherry picker was blocking a couple of car parking spaces and access to the bins.

With no response from Aldi, she decided to post on social media.

"I thought 'oh well, you know, they're great on social media, let's do a bit of a post on social media just to give them, you know, a little bit of a taste of their own medicine and see'," she said.

The practice first of all pretended to be concerned the picker "might be the start of your famous middle aisle expanding into our premises", then made a tongue-in-cheek offer to buy the machine "if it's under £49.99".

But when Aldi did not reply, the vets complained of being ghosted and joked about the stress on its "communications team" which, it said, consisted of "one increasingly frazzled vet who should probably be doing something more productive".

"[And] Timmy, a Norfolk Terrier with approximately one functioning brain cell, who is technically 'Head of Communications' but keeps eating the minutes of our meetings," it said.

Still getting no response, the team teased with a scenario where Aldi's Kevin the Carrot and Cauli dog had a Christmas emergency.

"It's Christmas Eve. Cauli Dog has eaten the Christmas tree. Kevin is panicking. The entire vegetable family rushes to the vets next door," it said.

"AND THEY CAN'T PARK BECAUSE ALDI HAVE LEFT A GIANT BLUE CHERRY PICKER IN OUR CAR PARK."

The posts have gained tens of thousands of like and comments.

On Friday, Aldi finally responded with: "Well, Derwent Valley Vets, we owe you a HUGE apology for leaving the Shiny Blue Lifty McLiftface in your car park. Sorry for leaving you waiting for a reply... but we want to make it right.

"So, as well as shifting the cherry picker (someone is moving it as we speak!) we'd love to donate a woofing big hamper of pet food to a local shelter of your choice. Just tell them Santa Paws has come early."

Goodear said: "It's sort of blown up far more than expected and seems to have reached many corners of the globe, with people commenting from Australia, Canada, all sorts of places, but we certainly weren't expecting.

"Yes, I think, I hope it's positive for everyone involved, the cherry picker has been safely collected and departed, and Aldi have very kindly dropped off a hamper for my team with biscuits and goodies and things, and also a hamper for Ashbourne Animal Welfare, which is a local rescue charity that we support."

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday hailed the court's intervention in the restrictions imposed on his movement in Leh. He said that the administration withdrew police personnel deployed outside his residence only after the matter came up for hearing.Joining the Leh Apex Body (LAB)-led protest, Wangchuk said he had been under effective house arrest since November 11 and appealed to President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to uphold constitutional values and democratic freedoms."India is not a rogue state. It is the world's largest democracy, and it has certain constitutional values and standards that must be upheld," Wangchuk said at a press conference with LAB chairman Chering Dorje Lakruk.His remarks came a day after Leh district police withdrew the arrangements made outside his residence to ensure compliance with a prohibitory order. The police, however, denied that Wangchuk had been placed under house arrest.In a post on X, Leh district police said, "Police arrangements which (were) placed to ensure compliance with prohibitory order have been withdrawn. ADM (Additional District magistrate), Leh has passed a prohibitory order against Wangchuk. It is clarified that he was not put under any house arrest as has been claimed."Wangchuk questioned the police's explanation, alleging that the administration was denying restrictions on his movement despite having deployed personnel outside his residence."This is an extremely strange way for a government to function. The State is behaving like a rogue state, where anyone can simply be picked up and detained. But when it is required to face the truth in a court of law, it suddenly claims that nothing happened and that there was no such detention," he said, referring to his earlier arrest under the National Security Act (NSA).Wangchuk recounts events leading to court proceedingsRecounting the events of November 11, Wangchuk alleged that he was forcibly picked up while preparations were underway for an indefinite protest. The demonstration was planned to press for the resumption of dialogue with the Centre and seek a deferment of the Hill Council elections scheduled for December 4."Those who came were wearing masks and hoodies, with their faces concealed. I would hesitate to even call them policemen because they looked more like goons," he said.Wangchuk claimed that although he had agreed to go to jail, he was instead taken to his residence at the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Ladakh (HIAL). He alleged that nearly two dozen local police and CRPF personnel, dressed in commando fatigues and carrying firearms, were deployed there.The activist said he subsequently decided to challenge the restrictions through legal channels, with the help of lawyers in Delhi and Ladakh.According to Wangchuk, an appeal was filed before the High Court bench in Leh on November 17 and listed for hearing the following day. He claimed that no government representative appeared during the November 18 hearing. The court then gave the government time until November 19 to submit its response.He said Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta appeared before the court on November 19 and sought time until November 23, which was granted."Taking advantage of this time, the authorities withdrew all the personnel deployed outside my residence Friday night," Wangchuk said.Wangchuk appeals to President, PMWangchuk also expressed concern over the alleged use of police personnel and government officials to carry out actions that could compromise their professional responsibilities."I hope that when they joined the civil services, whether the IPS or IAS, they did so with great aspirations and a genuine desire to serve the country. Today, however, they are being used and misused like pawns in what resembles a mafia gang," he said.Appealing to people across the country, he urged the government to ensure that officials and police personnel were allowed to perform their duties within the bounds of the law."I have appealed to President Murmu and the prime minister to put an end to this lawlessness and ensure that our officers and police personnel are allowed to discharge their duties with dignity and within the bounds of the law," he said.Wangchuk also defended the ongoing sit-in, saying he had joined his colleagues at the protest site. He said the demonstration had continued for 10 days and was peaceful and authorised.Wangchuk renews opposition to winter Hill Council pollsThe activist also reiterated his opposition to holding the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) elections during winter. He argued that a significant section of the population would be outside Ladakh during the season and would not be able to participate."On the one hand, we send a message to the world that we take democracy to the last citizen, even flying helicopters to polling stations where there are just two voters. On the other hand, we are excluding 40 to 50 per cent of the population and conducting elections during winter, amid snowfall, while also subjecting government officials to immense hardship," he said.Wangchuk clarified that people were not opposed to elections but wanted them held during a season that would allow wider public participation. He also pointed to the difficulties of deploying government officials in remote and snowbound areas during winter.He urged the government to reconsider the schedule and ensure that democratic processes in Ladakh remained inclusive rather than being imposed on the people.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Three summits, few wins: How Xi Jinping has kept Donald Trump waiting
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has held three high-profile meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping this year, but the summits have yielded few concrete
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has held three high-profile meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping this year, but the summits have yielded few concrete gains for Washington. Xi, meanwhile, has used the engagements to strengthen China's position on the global stage and keep key negotiations with the US on hold. Analysts say Beijing is gaining strategic room as Trump continues to seek progress on trade, technology and other contentious issues.The latest meeting took place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China this week. Trump described Xi's airport welcome as "a big win", but analysts said the fanfare surrounding the visit had not translated into significant concessions from Beijing.Xi gains diplomatic ground as Trump seeks concessionsXi broke with protocol to receive Trump at Shenzhen airport ahead of Thursday's APEC summit. The two leaders shared a hug and later held a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, the first of its kind involving the three countries.The meeting with Putin was a key part of Trump's agenda. The three leaders released a joint "Declaration Toward Peace", which analysts described as vague. Hosting the gathering also gave Xi an opportunity to project China as a central player in global affairs.Trump said he and Xi discussed artificial intelligence, trade and oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.Washington has been pressing China to increase purchases of American agricultural products, ease restrictions on rare-earth minerals and secure the release of two Americans it says are wrongfully detained.China's foreign ministry said the two sides agreed to work on an action plan to build a "constructive relationship of strategic stability". However, it provided no details or timeline. The framework had already been announced in May.Beijing's official account of the meeting did not mention the trade truce, agricultural commitments, rare-earth shipments, chip restrictions or the two detained Americans. It also made no reference to Iran.China is on track to meet its soybean purchase commitment for 2026 but has fulfilled only a fraction of its other promised agricultural purchases. Rare-earth shipments also remain well below levels recorded before the trade conflict escalated last year. Neither of the detained Americans has been released.Xi also reiterated Beijing's position on Taiwan, asking Washington to "keep doing the right thing" on the issue or risk setbacks in bilateral ties. China claims the democratically governed island as its territory, a position rejected by Taipei.China waits as US tightens chip restrictionsWhile Beijing has been in no hurry to meet Washington's demands, the Trump administration has moved to tighten restrictions on China's access to advanced technology.Following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang earlier this month, the US administration has sought to close loopholes that allow Chinese companies to bypass restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips.A new US rule further restricting China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia took effect on the day Trump and Xi met. Washington is also considering a rule that would require American companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models.US lawmakers have stepped up pressure as well. A House of Representatives committee report this week called for restrictions on investments in China's aerospace sector. A senator also introduced legislation seeking to revoke China's normal trade status and favourable tariff treatment.Beijing has vowed to retaliate against technology restrictions while seeking to keep bilateral relations stable. Analysts say China is unlikely to make all the concessions sought by Washington at once."The Chinese see these noises as a natural part of the relationship," news agency Reuters quoted Shen Weizhong saying, who is a former Chinese foreign ministry official."The Chinese have learned their lesson: they won't fulfil their side of a promise all at once. They'll do it step by step," he said.By holding back concessions, Beijing can retain leverage if Washington takes a tougher approach. Pressure on China is also growing in the US Congress, with lawmakers from both parties pushing for stronger measures.The US-China trade truce is expected to remain in place until the two leaders meet again at the Group of 20 summit in Miami next month. The truce, first reached at a meeting in South Korea last year and extended during Xi's visit to Washington in September, is due to expire on January 10.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Saturday took a swipe at Meta, saying the social media giant should now realise the consequences of promoting \"demons
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Saturday took a swipe at Meta, saying the social media giant should now realise the consequences of promoting "demons and monsters".His remarks came after the Indian Youth Congress (IYC), the Congress' youth wing, staged a protest outside Meta's offices in India, alleging that the accounts of its leaders had been suspended at the behest of the ruling BJP.Dubey, however, claimed that Meta had designed its algorithms to favour the Congress."There is a lesson here for Meta. The algorithm they have designed is tailored in favour of the Congress," PTI quoted the BJP MP as saying."When you promote 'rakshas' (demons) and 'danav' (monsters), what else do you expect the outcome to be? Meta, including X and Facebook, needs to understand this," he added.Meanwhile, the IYC issued a seven-day "ultimatum" to Meta, demanding that it restore restricted accounts and posts within the deadline.The IYC's warning came amid allegations that Meta, which owns Instagram, had suspended or restricted accounts and removed posts belonging to key party functionaries, including national president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma.On Friday, Telangana Youth Congress workers protested at Meta's Hyderabad office, accusing the company of "censorship." Around 20 protesters were taken into preventive custody and released after approximately three hours.Similar demonstrations were reported in Mumbai and Gurugram. The IYC also threatened to stage protests at Meta offices across the country if the restrictions were not lifted.The organisation demanded that Meta restore access to the accounts of opposition leaders, journalists and influencers within seven days, alleging that the company was favouring the BJP.(With agency inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Could Iran reverse its stated policy of a civil-only nuclear programme?
articles.summary: Iran’s FM Araghchi says there is ‘major strategic debate’ about the future of Iran’s nuclear doctrine.
articles.body:
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said the country’s stockpile of enriched uranium will be used according to its needs, “however they are defined”, as he spoke about possible changes to Iran’s longstanding nuclear doctrine.

Araghchi’s comments during an interview with Iranian media on Saturday have increased speculation that Iran may be moving away from its policy of limiting its nuclear programme to civilian purposes amid its conflict with the United States.

The future of Iran’s nuclear programme has become a major sticking point in efforts to end the war, with Washington insisting that it must have guarantees that Iran will never develop a nuclear weapon before it will agree to a full ceasefire.

So, is Iran’s nuclear policy changing, and what could that mean for the conflict?

Iran has consistently maintained that its nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes only, such as for electricity generation, medical research and agriculture.

This policy has been underlined by a decades-old religious decree, or fatwa, issued by the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, banning the development of nuclear weapons.

However, Iran has also insisted it has the right to enrich uranium for these purposes under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), which it joined in 1970. It has called this right “non-negotiable”.

What have Araghchi and other officials said?

In an interview with Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency on Saturday, Araghchi reiterated that Iran’s stockpile of enriched material would remain inside the country .

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) estimated in 2025 – before Israel launched strikes on Iran in June that year – that Iran had about 440 kilogrammes (970 pounds) of uranium enriched to about 60 percent. This is short of the 90 percent required for making nuclear weapons, but is the level at which it becomes much quicker to reach 90 percent. It is also far beyond the roughly 3 percent needed for power generation.

This material, Araghchi said during his interview, would “be used according to our needs however those needs are defined”.

Araghchi also made reference to an ongoing debate among lawmakers and officials in Iran about altering its nuclear doctrine, and said people on both sides of that debate have “strong arguments”.

“This is a major strategic debate, and there is nothing wrong with examining it seriously because it directly concerns national interests and security,” Araghchi said, adding that those in favour of reform argue Iran’s current approach of no nuclear weapons has “failed to protect” the country’s nuclear facilities, which have come under attack from US and Israeli forces both last year and this year.

However, Araghchi acknowledged that any official change to the policy would have “far-reaching consequences”.

“For now, our doctrine has not changed, and our official position remains the same,” he said.

Other Iranian officials have also spoken about a potential review of the country’s nuclear doctrine. Earlier this month, security chief Mohsen Rezaei said “there is a discussion on whether we want to continue to follow the previous nuclear doctrine in the event of a new war breaking out”, though he also stressed that Tehran has not yet made any change.

On November 12, Iran’s Assembly of Experts, the body that appoints the supreme leader, said reviewing “the country’s defence doctrine and establishing the necessary deterrence have become unavoidable necessities”.

Ali Fathollah-Nejad, a German-Iranian political scientist who directs the Center for Middle East and Global Order (CMEG), told Al Jazeera the move by the Assembly of Experts “appears to mark the first time a governing institution has endorsed this position”.

Why do the US and Israel think Iran is developing nuclear weapons?

Besides being a signatory to the NPT in 1970, Iran also initially complied with a nuclear agreement it struck with the US and other global powers in 2015 – the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), which required it to limit uranium enrichment to very low levels and undergo inspections.

But after Washington pulled out of the deal in 2018 under the first administration of US President Donald Trump, Tehran eventually went back to intensifying its nuclear programme and abandoned restrictions imposed by the deal.

In June 2025, the IAEA’s board of governors declared Iran was no longer complying with its commitment to international nuclear safeguards. Tehran rejected that report and accused the IAEA of giving a pretext for US and Israeli attacks targeting Iranian nuclear facilities, including Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, just days later during the 12-day war.

In March of this year, IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said at least 200kg (440lbs) of Iran’s enriched material was believed to have survived the US-Israeli attacks and was likely buried underground in or near the Isfahan nuclear facility site.

Grossi has since said the agency cannot verify the amount or location of Iran’s enriched material due to a lack of access.

The IAEA has called Iran’s enrichment level “a matter of serious concern”, while the US has pointed to it as evidence that Iran is pursuing nuclear weapons despite its official policy.

“If you don’t want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60 percent enriched fuel?” US Vice President JD Vance said in an interview with the Reuters news agency last month. “And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don’t build highly enriched fuel. That’s a very basic threshold issue.”

President Trump has repeatedly stated that Iran must never be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon.

Officials in Israel, which is widely believed to have its own undeclared nuclear weapons , have also long accused Iran of pursuing nuclear weapons.

“The Iranian regime, which seeks to destroy Israel, is once again working to revive its nuclear programme,” said Israel’s now-caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an address last week. “We must remove this existential threat once and for all.”

Will Iran officially reverse its no-nuclear-weapons policy?

That remains to be seen, but it is “within the realm of possibility”, Rouzbeh Parsi, an Iran analyst and affiliated researcher at Lund University’s Department of History and Human Rights Studies, told Al Jazeera.

He said the US-Israeli war launched against Iran in February this year “has significantly changed all the calculations in Tehran”, with more open discussion about whether to renew the late ayatollah’s ban on nuclear weapons now taking place.

“What used to be a fringe opinion, leaving the NPT and potentially going for a nuclear weapon, is now something that’s within the realm of possibility – even though all the major players are still warning against it,” said Parsi. “It’s not a decision but an indication that deterrence is being rethought in light of the war.”

Simon Mabon, a professor of international politics at Lancaster University, told Al Jazeera that a “broadly rational defensive reason” for potentially shifting Iran’s nuclear policy is emerging within the country, though adding that such a shift would be legally and ethically problematic.

“If you look at the sort of traditional nuclear logic, it says that nuclear weapons play a very strong defensive role in deterring the actions of another state,” Mabon told Al Jazeera. “That would be very sound logic for the Iranians in light of what’s happened.”

“This, of course, is something that’s deeply problematic,” said Mabon. “It goes against the terms of the NPT, it goes against the spirit of the NPT, so it would necessitate withdrawal from that.”

CMEG director Fathollah-Nejad said that there are serious divisions within Iran’s government over the direction of its nuclear programme.

Hardline lawmakers and religious leaders view Iran’s nuclear and missile assets as “indispensable” to “regime security and deterrence”, while a separate camp that includes former Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif argues against the development of nuclear arms, saying it would “almost inevitably” trigger further attacks by the US and Israel, said Fathollah-Nejad.

For now, he added, Iran “plays with the ambiguity” of its nuclear policy.

What does this mean for US-Iran negotiations?

Fathollah-Nejad said a shift in Iran’s nuclear doctrine would directly counter the US’s “single most important goal” in the conflict: to secure nuclear concessions from Tehran.

The US has insisted Iran must make nuclear commitments at the outset of any negotiations, while Iran wants its own seven stated conditions met, including lifting the blockade, restoring access to its frozen assets and ending hostilities on all fronts, before even beginning discussions about its nuclear programme.

Mabon said a change in Iran’s nuclear policy “would have a dramatic impact on how the Americans and the Israelis read the next phase of this conflict”, with the Israelis likely believing it necessitates a “return to violence”.

“That’s where some of the other dangers start to come in,” Mabon added. “The shift in Iran’s doctrine, even if it’s meant intentionally as a defensive shift, can easily be read in offensive terms.”

“I think it’s a very, very dangerous moment,” he said.

articles.title: Independent review ordered into surgery carried out by NHS Grampian
articles.summary: It follows a whistleblower's leaking of a document which shows there were 19 avoidable deaths at the health board.
articles.body:
The Scottish government has ordered a review into hepatobiliary surgery at NHS Grampian after a whistleblower leaked a document showing 19 avoidable deaths at the health board.

Dr Mohammed Habib claimed he had contacted the Scottish government on four separate occasions and had gone to the police and the lord advocate with his concerns about patient safety at the board.

In a report from 2022, which was only released by Habib on Thursday, it was found 19 of the 31 deaths in liver and pancreatic surgery cases were avoidable.

NHS Grampian chief executive, Laura Skaife-Knight, said the board would be "open and transparent" in co-operating with the review.

Habib also said two people had died after having the wrong procedure performed on them and has called for the health board to face a corporate homicide inquiry.

Health Secretary Angela Constance said the review would assess how concerns raised about liver, gallbladder and bile duct surgery, including those by Habib, were handled by the board and the Scottish government.

She said it would identify weaknesses in governance, missed opportunities, unreasonable delay, and gaps in accountability.

Constance said Habib's concerns were "deeply concerning and of the utmost seriousness".

"Following discussion with the first minister, I am today commissioning an urgent and fully independent review of how concerns about hepatobiliary (HPB) surgery in NHS Grampian was handled, including the 2022 report into the deaths of patients who underwent HPB surgery," she said.

"Patient safety and high-quality care must always be the first concern of all those who work in, and with, the NHS."

She said that if any patients had questions or needed advice and support they should contact the NHS Grampian helpline on 08085 202030.

One patient told BBC Scotland News he "technically died" after undergoing liver surgery at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary.

Derek Appleton said he believed mistakes had been made during a procedure to remove 60% of his liver after being diagnosed with stage four cancer.

He said he lost 11 litres of blood and went into cardiac arrest, but was never given a proper explanation for what happened.

Constance will make a statement in Holyrood on Tuesday, where she is expected to lay out the timetable and announce who will lead the review.

She said: "My thoughts are with anyone who has lost a loved one and I am acutely aware of the courage it has taken Dr Habib to come forward.

"I recognise he has sought to do this repeatedly, over a number of years, to both to the Scottish government and several other bodies.

"Patients and staff in Grampian have the right to expect full transparency and independent assurance that when valid concerns are raised, they are properly and robustly pursued. That is what this review will seek to establish."

Skaife-Knight said the review was the "best way forward".

She added: "We know the allegations which have been the subject of significant media interest in recent days will cause further concern for patients and families, our communities and staff.

"We will take immediate steps to secure and preserve relevant information, files and records as part of this process."

Humza Yousaf was health secretary at the time of Dr Habib's report.

He told BBC Scotland News he supported "further dramatic action" being taken in relation to NHS Grampian.

A spokesperson for Yousaf - who went on to become first minister before resigning in May 2024 – said: "Humza supports full transparency about what happened at NHS Grampian and will co-operate fully with any review that takes place.

"He has made it clear that he supports minutes from the period in question being released.

"As health secretary, Humza met whistleblowing champions in health boards across Scotland, and he remains clear that staff who raise patient safety concerns must be listened to and protected.

"It takes real courage to do what Dr Habib has done, and he should be commended for refusing to let these concerns go."

The Scottish government has said action will be taken quickly when required as part of the process to refer any issues – including potential criminality – to the relevant authorities without waiting for the final report.

The announcement comes after First Minister John Swinney announced a review of how the government handles correspondence, after he claimed he first heard of three letters sent to him by Habib on Thursday.

On Tuesday, Constance appointed an expert health team to oversee NHS Grampian improvements.

She said the "external intervention support team", comprising experienced senior NHS leaders, would work alongside Grampian's health team to provide "intensive turnaround support".

Healthcare Improvement Scotland has also been asked to complete an early review of NHS Grampian within three months to assess progress, followed by ongoing reviews, to provide independent assurance.

Scottish Labour's health spokeswoman, Jackie Baillie, said the review was "welcome", adding that a similar situation "must never happen ever again".

She said: "Were it not for the bravery of Dr Habib in this week speaking out, we may never have known just how far this went.

"Grieving families who lost loved ones in the care of NHS Grampian deserve the full truth of what happened at the health board, including who knew what was going on, when they knew, and why it has taken this long for these concerns to come to light."

Yi-pei Chou Turvey, Scottish Liberal Democrat MSP for north east Scotland, said the wait for answers for the families of affected patients had been "excruciating".

She added: "SNP ministers ought to have been battering down the door of NHS Grampian after receiving multiple warnings from Dr Habib and a report uncovering 19 avoidable deaths.

"This independent review must quickly and thoroughly establish why John Swinney, Humza Yousaf and successive health secretaries failed to grasp what was going on and intervene."

Scottish Conservative health spokesman Miles Briggs said the review should not be used as a "vehicle to shirk responsibility".

"This review must determine exactly what information reached Scottish ministers and NHS Grampian executives and what action was taken," he said.

"For patients and their families, the review must follow the evidence wherever it leads and ensure full accountability at every level."
