articles.title: History buff links prominent colonial New Yorker to notorious pirate heist
articles.summary: Amateur historian James Bailey says colonial records suggest Thomas Jones, the namesake of Jones Beach, helped pirate Capt. Henry Every dodge authorities.
articles.body: An amateur historian believes he's found clues suggesting a link between a notorious 17th-century pirate and the namesake of New York's famous Jones Beach — and says he has the documents to back it up. James Bailey, who found ancient coins linked to pirate Capt. Henry Every — known as the "King of the Pirates" — in 2014, recently said colonial-era records suggest Every and his crew got an assist from Thomas Jones, the namesake of the Long Island state park, The Associated Press (AP) reported. Bailey was metal detecting at Sweet Berry Farm, a fruit orchard in Middletown, Rhode Island, when he unearthed an Every-linked 17th-century Arabian coin over a decade ago. TREASURE HUNTERS FIND BIGGEST VIKING COIN HOARD IN COUNTRY'S HISTORY: 'WITHOUT PARALLEL' It wasn't until 2021 that Bailey publicized his discovery to the AP and dug deeper into colonial records — which led him to do further research on Every and Jones. Every is best known for leading the 1695 raid on the royal Indian treasure ship Ganj-i-Sawai in the Red Sea — making off with tens of millions of dollars in gold and silver before vanishing in what some consider the first worldwide manhunt. Bailey — whose claims are not yet independently verified — said documents suggest Jones was recruited to serve as a "wheelman" for Every and help the crew steer clear of authorities. "You have millions of visitors and generations of New Yorkers going to this beach," Bailey told the AP. TREASURE HUNTERS RECOVER RARE SILVER BAR FROM LEGENDARY SHIPWRECK OFF FLORIDA KEYS "Nobody knew he was actually a major player in arguably the biggest heist in the history of piracy." Even during his lifetime, a document showed that New York's governor investigated Jones after he had already become the proprietor of a whaling operation, AP reported. Jones was born in Ireland and moved to Rhode Island and New York before acquiring acres of land that now comprise Jones Beach. How exactly he made his fortune was considered a mystery both now and after his death. REVOLUTIONARY WAR ARTIFACTS UNEARTHED AT SITE OF INFAMOUS COLONIAL AMERICAN HEIST: 'VERY SURPRISED' In 1906, one of his descendants addressed the rumors that Jones was a pirate, calling them "slander" and "improbable fictions." "People were disposed to cast slurs upon his memory, either for mischievousness, or a spirit of malice," the writer, Thomas Floyd-Jones, said at the time. "The reality was that privateers were pirates, just sponsored by a certain government or patron." He added, "These myths were cherished for over a century after his death, which ignorance and superstition did not fail to magnify." Meagan Schulman, a Fordham University doctoral candidate who specializes in 17th-century piracy and was not involved in the research, told the AP that, since Jones was already a privateer authorized to raid commercial ships of rivals, he could already be considered a pirate. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER It was only when war ended that those who continued to do so were called pirates. "The reality was that privateers were pirates, just sponsored by a certain government or patron," said Schulman, as the AP reported. "So maybe the short answer is, yes. Jones can be called a pirate, by some people, but he probably did not ever see himself as one." Part of Jones' wealth came when his father-in-law gifted him a lot of land — something Bailey suggests gave him a fresh start. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Richard Blakemore, a maritime history professor at the University of Reading in the United Kingdom, told the AP that Bailey's research is persuasive but not yet definitive. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ He added that the records point to how deeply early British colonies were intertwined with piracy. "Popular images of pirates show them as outcasts, but many historians have argued the opposite, based on evidence like this," Blakemore said. articles.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping
articles.summary: British maritime agency reports two incidents near Oman, while Iran says a tanker caught fire due to naval mine.
articles.body:
British maritime authorities have reported two incidents involving tankers struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz, as Iran continues to restrict shipping through the vital waterway.

The incidents were reported on Saturday near Oman, amid a war involving Tehran, Washington and Tel Aviv that began with the United States and Israel attacking Iran in late February.

Tehran has since sought to tighten its control over the strait, which carried nearly a fifth of the world’s crude oil supplies before the conflict.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre, a British agency that monitors threats to commercial shipping, said one tanker was hit at its rear about 20km (13 miles) north of Khasab, a port town on Oman’s northern coast.

Another tanker was struck in its engine room about 31km (20 miles) east of Khasab, the agency said.

No casualties were reported, but it remained unclear whether the two incidents involved separate vessels.

Iran’s navy said on Saturday that an oil tanker had caught fire after striking a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait.

In a statement carried by Iranian state television, the navy accused the vessel of ignoring warnings and travelling with its identification and navigation equipment switched off.

The Iranian account could not be independently verified, and it was unclear whether the burning tanker was involved in either incident reported by UKMTO.

Al Jazeera’s correspondent in Tehran, Resul Serdar, said incidents involving tankers had increased sharply over the past week.

Citing statements issued by Iran’s armed forces, Serdar said about 25 incidents had been reported since the previous Saturday, averaging roughly three a day, a trend he called “quite dramatic”.

“This is becoming a pattern,” Serdar said, explaining that “Iranians are saying the Strait of Hormuz is under their control; that any ship that is passing through the Strait of Hormuz has to be in full coordination with the Iranian authorities and must follow the roads and the lanes that are determined by Iran.”

If ships do not comply, Iran says “they are either going to be attacked, or they are going to hit the sea mines that are laid by the [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] IRGC or the Iranian forces”, Serdar added.

Our correspondent said Tehran was deliberately escalating tensions to send a message that if Iran could not export its oil, other countries would not be able to do so either.

He said Iran was also seeking to show that it remained in control of the strait, a narrow passage connecting the Gulf with international shipping routes.

The US has responded to Iran’s restrictions by blockading Iranian ports and deploying naval vessels to escort tankers through the waterway.

The confrontation has raised concerns over the security of a major route for global energy supplies, with commercial vessels caught in the struggle between Washington and Tehran over access to the strait.

articles.title: A film crew spotted 5-year-old Judith Barsi skating at an ice rink; after she was killed at 10, audiences heard her voice as Ducky in The Land Before Time
articles.summary: Discover the heartbreaking story of Judith Barsi, the talented child actress whose life was cut short by her father's violent actions. Best known for her role as Ducky in 'The Land Before Time', her tragic journey from ice skating star to murder victim reveals a dark side of Hollywood.
articles.body: Throughout the history of film and television, many actors met tragic ends in accidents or through struggles with illness, addiction, or mental health. One was child actress Judith Eva Barsi, who was murdered by her own father. Throughout her short career, Judith appeared in 72 commercials alongside several movies and television shows, according to the Los Angeles Times. She was best known as the voice of Ducky in the animated film The Land Before Time, and Anne-Marie in All Dogs Go to Heaven.Both animated films were released posthumously. Furthermore, she appeared in several television shows, including Growing Pains and St. Elsewhere.Judith was born on June 6, 1978, in Los Angeles to Hungarian immigrants, Maria and József Barsi. Maria began preparing her daughter Judith for an acting career early on by teaching her poise, posture, and vocal skills. At age 5, Judith was reportedly discovered by a commercial film crew at an ice skating rink. Due to her petite frame, the crew mistook her for a 3-year-old, and that worked out in her favor.From a young age, Judith showcased natural talent, bagging her first credited role in the drama miniseries Fatal Vision, playing Kimberly MacDonald. Soon after, she became a sought-after child actress in Hollywood. A major turning point in her acting career came when she got the role of Thea Brody in the 1987 film Jaws: The Revenge. She subsequently voiced the character of Ducky in The Land Before Time, and Anne-Marie in All Dogs Go to Heaven, which marked her final film role.Escalating tensions behind closed doorsJudith had a tumultuous family life. As per those close to the Barsi family, Judith’s father József had a controlling nature and often made terrifying threats. As Judith continued to make a mark in Hollywood, her father’s rage and jealousy also increased over time.The publication reported that before Judith left for the Bahamas to shoot Jaws: The Revenge, her father held a knife to her throat and threatened to kill her if she didn’t return. Eventually, Judith began showing signs of extreme distress, including pulling out her own eyelashes, and she confided to family friends that she was afraid to go back home.In December 1986, Maria reached out to the Los Angeles County Department of Children’s Services and reported József’s threats, but the case was shut down after police found no visible injuries, and Maria ultimately decided not to prosecute. Neighbors and friends recalled how Maria had been taking steps to leave József, like renting an apartment in Panorama City, but was still hesitant to take the final leap.The July 1988 tragedyBefore Maria could complete the move, the abuse turned fatal. As cited in the records shared by the Los Angeles Times, Judith and her mother, Maria, were killed by József in their West Hills, California, home on July 25, 1988. József shot Maria in the hallway of their home and Judith in her bed.After the murders, József doused their bodies and the house with gasoline, lighting the house on fire before taking his own life in the garage. Once the firefighters arrived at the crime scene, they extinguished the blaze. Shortly afterwards, the police officials discovered Judith’s body in her bedroom near a pink television that her father had reportedly given as a misguided apology for previous abuse.You use AI every day. articles.title: David McKittrick: Former journalist and Lost Lives author dies
articles.summary: David McKittrick was best known for his work during the Troubles, and his book Lost Lives.
articles.body:
The renowned journalist and author David McKittrick has died at the age of 77.

McKittrick was best known for his work during the Troubles, and the book Lost Lives.

The book detailed the people who died as a result of the Troubles.

It was first published in 1999 after several years of research by McKittrick and co-authors Seamus Kelters, Brian Feeney and Chris Thornton.

Lost Lives won the Ewart-Biggs Memorial Prize for the promotion of peace and understanding in 2000.

At a later stage, David McVea joined the project.

A death notice for McKittrick said he was the "beloved husband of Pat, much loved father of Julie and Kerry, cherished grandfather of Daniel and Emma and the dear brother of Arlene and Freda".

"He will be sorely missed by all his extended family and friends," it added.

Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) leader Claire Hanna MP paid tribute to McKittrick, describing him as an "outstanding journalist".

"David McKittrick was the outstanding journalist reporting in Northern Ireland throughout the Troubles," she said.

"Calm, empathetic and rigorous, he combined exceptional integrity with an unrivalled network of contacts.

"Throughout decades of conflict, he preserved his humanity and remained true to his moral compass."

Hanna added that her "thoughts are with David's family, friends and former colleagues at this sad time".

Journalist and author Eamonn Mallie was friends with McKittrick for over 40 years and they co-authored three books together.

Mallie said McKittrick came from a very modest upbringing, but "nobody in my opinion in journalism, in my generation, emulated his capacity".

"He had a way with words which were so natural and so unique."

Mallie said McKittrick "wrote beautifully" and it was "a wonderful experience" to co-author the books with him.

He described McKittrick him as a "giant of journalism" and as "quirky, alternative, a beautiful gentleman".

McKittrick reported on the Troubles in Northern Ireland since the 1970s.

The Belfast-born author wrote for the East Antrim Times and later joined the Irish Times in 1973 as a reporter in Belfast, becoming northern editor in 1976 and London editor in 1981.

He also briefly worked for BBC Northern Ireland in 1985 before joining the The Independent (London) in 1986.

McKittrick then worked as The Independent's Irish correspondent for many years, while contributing to overseas newspapers and journals.

His awards include an Orwell Prize for Journalism, 2000, the Christopher Ewart-Biggs Memorial Prize in 1988, and Correspondent of the Year, 1999.

Another one of McKittrick's most-read books is Making Sense of the Troubles.

First published in 2000 and co-authored with historian David McVea, the book delves into the roots of the conflict from the partition of Ireland in 1921, the descent into violence in the late 60s and the three decades of unrest that followed.

articles.title: Trumpiana: Trifecta tumble, troika, trash tantrums!
articles.summary: With two legs of his power trifecta tumbling under a Democratic blue midterm tsunami, Donald Trump embarked on an 8,000 mile odyssey to conquer the world
articles.body: With two legs of his power trifecta tumbling under a Democratic blue midterm tsunami, Donald Trump embarked on an 8,000 mile odyssey to conquer the world on his new opulent palace in the sky.Returning home after a historic troika with pals, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, on the new $400 million Air Force One gifted by Qatar — without the Turkish caper in July when he made a great escape in a catering truck — the POTUS praised the speed of his new ride.At a rambling 90-minute Oval Office press conference Friday, he gushed about Xi Jinping coming to greet him at Shenzhen airport — “He didn’t meet Sleepy Joe with the plane, that I can tell you,” and his friendship with Putin — he was “very nice about the fake Russia, Russia, Russia hoax,” — though he can’t “speak to America” for sure.Trump also touted the ‘great success’ of the summit that had been compared to Yalta in 1945 when Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill, and Joseph Stalin divided Europe, though his Shenzhen troika had nothing comparable to show.There was no deal on nuclear proliferation, trade or critical minerals or ending the wars in Iran — “They’ve been bullshitting people for 51 years,” — and Ukraine — blaming “tremendous hatred” between Putin and Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky.But standing in the company of two strongmen, Trump was sending a clear message: lame duck or not, he was still relevant!Then he stirred the succession pot turning the Oval Office presser into a virtual audition à la his Apprentice show between Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio before orchestrating a twist ending.But it was his new chief of staff, immigration hardliner Stephen Miller who stole the show in Trump’s eyes. “The most powerful man in the room right now,” Trump said of Miller. “He was better than these two guys. Do you want to run for president?” he joked.Asked how he planned to spend his final two years in office opposite a Democratic Congress, Trump laid out two futures for himself: As a bipartisan dealmaker, or a hardline issuer of vetoes. The choice would be up to Democrats, he insisted.“They could go two years and one month, because that’s what we have, and I’m going to veto them,” Trump said. But “if they want to get things done, I want to get things done.”The president also vowed to hit U.S. companies with a “tremendous tax” if they try to build data centers elsewhere, arguing that there is plenty of domestic demand for the structures powering the AI boom. “We’re going to fight very hard for the data centers,” he said going against strong public opinion.When at the end of the presser, an NBC reporter attempted to shout a question, Trump turned prickly again. “You’re a really rude person,” Trump told her. “So I’m not talking to you.”If only he could take a leaf out of the Chinese playbook. They had barred a Bloomberg News journalist from the trilateral meeting after asking Trump and Xi about Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and the spy scandal.Earlier, during Xi’s televised speech at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China, Trump appeared to doze off closing his eyes for about 10 seconds. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.As critics mocked Trump, White House officials dismissed it as “Fake News!” claiming the President “was looking at papers in front of him while the speaker made remarks. You can clearly see his eyes move back and forth.”And before embarking on the trip as planes stopped flying, Microsoft Outlook went down, Apple Pay froze up, and the NSA reported a mysterious system failure, Trump brushed off the whole affair as “fine.”“It’s life … When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen, it’s fine,” he said. Trump also blamed Biden for a rare nationwide ground stop saying, “Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad,” before finally ousting a top cybersecurity official.But he kept his focus on making Washington beautiful again with new White House renovation projects with renewed attention after the midterms with plans to reset stones in Lafayette Square and remake Rose Garden walkways.Trump lashed out at an NBC News reporter who asked if his construction projects were distracting him from other issues, calling her “pathetic” and suggesting she lacked “talent.”Defending his “flawless” White House renovations that he said cost “peanuts’’ Trump said, ‘’I have a responsibility to make sure the symbol of our country is in decent shape. It takes 10 minutes a day,” Trump said.“This doesn’t cost money. This is peanuts. And I pay for it. This doesn’t cost money. This is peanuts. This is called talent. …I spent very little time to do it and losers like you come out and say, ‘Why are you focused on the White House?’”Trump also lashed out at a Biden appointed judge for blocking reconstruction “of one of the worst and most dangerous golf courses anywhere in the U.S. ‘Trash Island,’ as it is affectionately known.”Complying with the judge’s order not to shut down East Potomac Golf Links, the Trump administration kept the property open but closed operations of the course.But even as the nonprofit that ran the golf course finished its final day of operating before its planned closure local enthusiasts didn’t let that stop them. They are continuing to play there taking care of the course themselves.So does Trump. Call him lame duck or Donald Duck, he would keep playing his game!(The article is an arrangement with The American Bazaar)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Second federal judge blocks Trump's proposed 250-foot Washington arch near Arlington National Cemetery, calling it a rushed job without congressional approval
articles.summary: A second federal judge has moved to stop construction of US President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery,
articles.body: A second federal judge has moved to stop construction of US President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery, ruling that the project lacked a clear legal basis and had not gone through the proper review process. The decision was delivered on Friday, 20 November 2026, in Alexandria, Virginia. According to Reuters, US District Judge Leonie Brinkema said the administration's efforts to approve the monument amounted to a "rushed job". She indicated that she would issue a preliminary injunction blocking construction while the legal challenge continues. The ruling is another setback for Trump's plan to build a large monument near the historic military cemetery. The proposed arch has faced opposition from local authorities, veterans, preservation groups and residents concerned about its size, location and impact on the surrounding area.The project has become the subject of several legal challenges. Brinkema's decision follows an earlier ruling by US District Judge Tanya Chutkan in Washington, DC, who temporarily stopped construction on 5 November. Chutkan later extended that restriction until 3 December while considering arguments for a longer-term ban, Reuters reported on 18 November. The Virginia ruling goes further by directly addressing a separate legal challenge brought by Arlington County. It prevents the administration from moving ahead with construction while Brinkema considers the county's case.Questions over legal authority and planningA major issue in the case is whether Trump has the legal power to build the monument without specific approval from Congress. The administration has argued that a law passed in 1925 gives it enough authority to proceed with the project. Brinkema rejected that argument during the hearing. According to Reuters, she questioned the government's reliance on the century-old law and said the project lacked congressional approval. "It hurts your credibility with the court by focusing on that," the judge told government lawyers. "This is a project that lacks congressional approval."The judge also raised concerns about the government's assessment of the project's possible effects on the surrounding area. She said federal officials had not properly examined its economic and environmental impact. One particular concern involved nearby Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. The proposed arch would stand around 3,000 feet from the airport, within its main approach and departure corridor. Although the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in September that the structure would not create a danger to aircraft, it required the monument to have a warning light at the top. Floodlights would also have to be directed towards the arch so pilots could see it.Trump has described the proposed structure as a "top-grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch". Some aviation experts have raised concerns about its location and possible effects on aircraft operations, Reuters reported. The FAA's requirements also mean the monument would need permanent lighting, adding another issue to the debate over its impact on the surrounding area.Community and historical oppositionThe size and location of the proposed monument have attracted criticism from local officials and people concerned about the historic setting around Arlington National Cemetery. At 250 feet (76 metres), the arch would be a major addition to the Washington area. Opponents argue that building such a large structure near the cemetery could affect the area's appearance and the experience of people visiting the site. Arlington County has challenged the federal government's decision to move ahead with the project. Its legal team argues that the approval process did not properly consider the effects on people who live and work in the area.Kate Talmor, a lawyer at Democracy Forward representing Arlington County, welcomed the Virginia judge's decision. "We are pleased that the court has recognized the irreparable harm that will come to people who live and work in Arlington and stopped the massive vanity project while our case is heard and considered by the court," Talmor said, according to Reuters. The opposition has also extended to members of the Kennedy family. Nine family members have joined efforts to stop the construction, arguing that the proposed arch would block views and cast shadows over the graves of their relatives at Arlington National Cemetery.The cemetery is a major national memorial and the resting place of American service members. Opponents believe the proposed structure could change the character of the surrounding landscape. The project has also faced wider criticism over the administration's decision to move forward while legal challenges remain unresolved.White House plans to continue defending the projectDespite the latest ruling, the Trump administration has indicated that it will continue fighting to secure approval for the monument. White House spokesman Davis Ingle criticised the legal challenge and defended the proposed structure as a tribute to the country. "The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation," Ingle said. "We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds." The White House has indicated that it intends to appeal the Virginia ruling, according to Reuters. The legal dispute forms part of a wider series of court challenges involving Trump's plans to reshape parts of Washington. Other projects that have faced scrutiny include renovations to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and a proposed championship-level golf course about two miles (3.22 kilometres) from the White House.For now, the proposed triumphal arch cannot move forward while the Virginia case is being considered. The separate Washington case also continues, with Judge Chutkan's temporary order remaining in place until 3 December. The two legal challenges raise questions about the limits of presidential authority over federal land and whether major national monuments can be approved without clear congressional backing. For Arlington County and other opponents, the immediate priority is preventing construction until the courts have fully considered the government's legal authority and the potential effects of the project. The White House, meanwhile, maintains that the arch is an appropriate national monument and says it will continue defending the plan in court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Cargo ship bound for Russia’s Kaliningrad hit by drones, Finland tightens security
articles.summary: A cargo ship bound for Russia’s Baltic exclave ​of Kaliningrad was struck by drones in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on ‌Saturday, Russian and Finnish authorities said, prompting Finland to tighten security measures in the area.
articles.body: A cargo ship bound for Russia’s Baltic exclave ​of Kaliningrad was struck by drones in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on ‌Saturday, Russian and Finnish authorities said, prompting Finland to tighten security measures in the area. The vessel was damaged west of Russia’s Gogland island, caught fire and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters, Finland’s Defense Forces said, corroborating an earlier account ​by Russian officials. Leningrad region Gov. Aleksandr Drozdenko said the vessel had been attacked by two drones ​in international waters about three nautical miles from Russia’s border. The crew was being ⁠evacuated and the extent of the damage was being assessed, he said. Finland’s defense ministry said the military ​had reintroduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution to protect ​civilians and enable authorities to operate if drones needed to be intercepted. Finland had informed its allies about the incident, the ministry said. Estonia’s Police and Border Guard Board said in an emailed statement it had been informed that a fire had broken ​out aboard the Russian cargo vessel Sparta II and that preliminary information indicated there had been explosions ​on board. “The war is spilling over into our neighboring areas. Finnish authorities are ‌handling the ⁠situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor,” Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X. “The situation poses no danger to other maritime traffic. ... Preparations for potential rescue operations are being made in cooperation with other ​authorities in Finland and internationally,” ​the Finnish Border Guard ⁠said in a statement. Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region and lifted a drone threat warning. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said ​on X his country was monitoring the situation and had offered help to ​its neighbor ⁠Finland, without giving details. Ukraine’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Kaliningrad Gov. Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region. Gogland lies in the eastern Gulf of Finland, about ⁠25 ​miles from Finland’s coast. Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave on the Baltic ​Sea between Poland and Lithuania that has occasionally been a flashpoint between Russia and NATO and the European Union.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war
articles.summary: Ocean campaigner Lewis Pugh completes Hormuz challenge and warns of lasting environmental damage.
articles.body:
A British endurance swimmer has completed a three-day swim through the Strait of Hormuz to draw attention to what he says is the environmental cost of the conflict involving Iran.

Lewis Pugh, who is a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam about 15km (9.3 miles) through the strategic waterway, a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East.

Pugh, 56, who was born in Plymouth, Devon said "war causes immense human suffering" but nature is "another casualty that receives far too little attention".

He is calling for an end to the fighting, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and action to address environmental damage caused by the conflict.

The swimmer is believed to be the first person to attempt a long-distance swim in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in March .

He swam from Musandam Island in the strait to the Cape of Hormuz, at the northern tip of Oman's Musandam Peninsula.

According to the Lewis Pugh Foundation, an oil tanker was struck by a projectile about 4km (2.5 miles) from where he was swimming on the first day.

On the second day, he saw flames rising above a headland separating him from the burning liquefied petroleum gas carrier Tara Gas and later passed close to the vessel while it was still on fire.

"My immediate thoughts were for the seafarers on board," Pugh said.

"The flames were enormous. These vessels carry highly flammable gases, and an attack on one can have catastrophic consequences - not just for crew members, but also on the surrounding marine environment."

Pugh said environmental damage caused by conflict often receives less attention than the human cost.

"War causes immense human suffering. Lives are lost, families are torn apart, and homes, hospitals and schools can be destroyed in minutes," he said.

"But there is another casualty that receives far too little attention: nature itself. And the damage can last long after the fighting has stopped."

The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping routes and is also home to wildlife including dugongs, sea turtles and whale sharks.

Pugh said oil spills and other contamination could have long-term consequences for marine ecosystems including coral reefs, seagrass meadows and mangrove forests.

articles.title: India’s opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals
articles.summary: Indian Youth Congress issues a seven-day ‘ultimatum’ to the US technology giant, urging it to lift all restrictions.
articles.body:
The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party has staged protests outside Meta offices in three cities, demanding that the United States technology company restore the Instagram accounts of its leaders.

The protests took place in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram, near New Delhi, on Friday and led to clashes with police and security guards, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress on Saturday.

In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building that houses Meta’s offices and clashed with police. In Mumbai, protesters spray-painted slogans on the walls outside, and in Gurugram they held banners reading “restore Youth Congress accounts”.

The party has alleged that on November 19, Meta illegally withheld the Instagram accounts of the youth wing’s president and the party official overseeing the wing on orders from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

In a statement accompanied by videos of the protests, the Congress youth wing said, “If Meta wants to do business in India, it must respect the Indian Constitution, not surrender to arbitrary BJP government orders.”

It had also warned Meta on X that it would “storm your offices across the country and stage protests” unless the accounts were restored.

Manu Jain, who runs the group’s social media, told the Reuters news agency on Saturday that two accounts were restored after Friday’s protests, but thousands of other accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government are still restricted.

The youth wing issued a seven-day “ultimatum” to the technology giant, urging it to lift all “restrictions on opposition voices, journalists and creators”.

It asked how many Indian accounts were withheld on government orders in the past six months, and how many remain blocked. It also asked Meta to explain what it called the automated blocking of posts that mention Congress leader Rahul Gandhi or criticise Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP.

On Saturday, the protesters also posted a video of workers putting up a banner in central Delhi that mocked Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, as “Mark BJPberg” – suggesting that Meta favours Modi’s party.

Meta has yet to issue a statement on the matter.

Police registered a complaint against four Youth Congress leaders in Mumbai and detained some protesters, Dainik Jagran English reported.

Pradeep Bhandari, a spokesperson for the ruling BJP, accused the protesters of vandalising Meta’s Hyderabad office and “flaunting it on social media”.

India is Meta’s biggest market by users.

In February, the government ordered platforms to remove unlawful content within three hours of notice, down from 36 hours. The government issued nearly 195,000 blocking orders to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July, the Indian Express reported.

Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025, according to its disclosures. It said most were cases in which it was “obligated to proactively restrict content” under local law.

articles.title: Viral frozen yogurt shop becomes Gen Z’s new neighborhood bar as young adults ditch booze
articles.summary: Mimi's frozen yogurt, a Gen Z Upper East Side and Greenwich Village hotspot, could rival Dorrian's as young New Yorkers skip alcohol this Thanksgiving Eve.
articles.body: For years, popular Manhattan bar Dorrian’s has been a Thanksgiving Eve staple, but some younger New Yorkers may be trading bar stools for a frozen treat as they ditch alcohol. Mimi’s, a frozen yogurt shop that has emerged as a see-and-be-seen destination for Gen Z and young adults, could also be a draw on Thanksgiving Eve, especially for people who want the buzz of a celebratory night out without going to a bar. Mimi's Upper East Side shop, near East 72nd Street and Lexington Avenue, and its Greenwich Village location have both become gathering spots for everyone from well-heeled teens with town cars awaiting them to couples to finance bros, Town & Country recently reported. The crowd also includes college students from nearby New York University and Parsons School of Design and off-duty doctors. HOME COCKTAIL MAKER SAYS GEN Z ISN'T GIVING UP ALCOHOL — THEY'RE CHANGING HOW THEY DRINK Founder Amber Linz opened Mimi’s as a pop-up in August 2025, hoping to bring New York the easygoing Australian café vibe she missed after moving to the city. She spent about a year developing its Greek yogurt-based frozen yogurt, made with real fruit purées and paired with seasonal toppings. The shop’s tart yogurt, attractive, exposed-wood interiors and social-media buzz are part of the draw, according to Town & Country. AMERICANS ARE PAYING PEOPLE TO WAIT IN LINE FOR TIKTOK-FAMOUS FOOD The appeal reflects a shift in how young people socialize. As more Gen Zers seek ways to go out that don't revolve around alcohol, bakeries, coffee shops and dessert spots are drawing them in. Town & Country likened the Upper East Side Mimi's to Dorrian's and the Village location to the nearby Red Lion. $20 FROZEN YOGURT? articles.title: 'Depends on how we settle up with Iran': Trump on rising fuel prices
articles.summary: US President Trump insists on a permanent agreement with Iran to prevent nuclear weapon development, highlighting mistrust in past negotiations and linking energy prices to diplomatic outcomes.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has said he wants a permanent agreement with Iran that prevents the country from developing nuclear weapons, warning that Washington will not accept a deal that fails to meet its demands.In an interview with Fox News on Saturday, Trump reiterated his position that any understanding with Tehran must provide lasting guarantees against its nuclear ambitions. He also questioned Iran's record in negotiations, accusing the country of repeatedly agreeing to terms before abandoning them."I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent. I'm not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon," Trump said.POTUS also played down the prospect of pursuing regime change in Iran, saying he had never been particularly interested in that objective. However, he described the attacks on the country's senior leadership as a significant development for Tehran.Trump characterised Iran's new leadership as "more rational" but expressed doubts about whether its representatives could be trusted during negotiations. He alleged that previous agreements with Iran had not delivered lasting results, reinforcing his demand for a deal that would prevent the country from obtaining nuclear weapons.His comments followed a press conference on Friday, after his visit to China, during which he criticised Tehran's negotiating position and accused it of misleading the international community for decades.Trump argued that Iran was interested in reaching an agreement but had not presented terms that Washington could accept. He also connected the movement in US gasoline prices to the outcome of the negotiations, suggesting that a settlement with Tehran could influence fuel costs."The prices of gasoline now, that also depends on how we settle up with Iran. They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me," Trump said.He added that Washington wanted an agreement that addressed its concerns rather than another arrangement that he believed would fail to deliver meaningful results."We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal that they've been doing for 51 years. No longer 47. People talk 47. It's 51 years," he said.Trump further accused Tehran of misleading people over the past five decades, saying: "They've been bullsh***ing people for 51 years."The latest remarks reflect the continuing disagreement between Washington and Tehran over the conditions required for a diplomatic settlement. Trump has repeatedly criticised the proposals put forward by Iran, maintaining that any agreement must satisfy US demands on its nuclear programme.The diplomatic dispute is unfolding amid wider tensions in West Asia. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly urged the Trump administration to consider renewed military action against Iran, adding another dimension to Washington's decisions on how to deal with Tehran.Although Trump has continued to express an interest in reaching an agreement, his latest statements indicate that he remains unwilling to accept a settlement that does not provide a lasting restriction on Iran's ability to develop nuclear weapons.You use AI every day. articles.title: JONATHAN TURLEY: Baltimore Raven learns truth is no defense in the NFL
articles.summary: Ravens star Marlon Humphrey was suspended over a four-word joke about Baltimore crime on his podcast, as Mayor Brandon Scott rejected his apology.
articles.body: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will not be playing this Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. He is not on the IL list, but on the FS list. Humphrey was flagged for free speech; uttering four words about the crime problem in Baltimore. The cornerback quipped that the city is "best at making criminals." While Ravens players were allowed to protest the United States at a London game, a player is not allowed to make a political comment on his personal podcast about the crime epidemic in his city. The day Humphrey was suspended, a 30-year-old woman was shot and killed near the M&T Bank Stadium. However, players would be wise not to acknowledge the crime. However, they could presumably condemn the country. Head Coach Jesse Minter announced that Humphrey had been suspended after the 10-year veteran spoke about crime in the city on his podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show. He was asked what Baltimore is best at making. Notably, Humphrey first offered The Star-Spangled Banner and National Bohemian beer. He then added as a joke that the city is also "best at making criminals." Crime in Baltimore makes the city one of the most dangerous cities in the United States. Despite a drop in crime levels, it remains in the top five cities for violent crime. WOMAN KILLED NEAR RAVENS STADIUM SAME DAY MARLON HUMPHREY SENT HOME FOR JOKE ABOUT BALTIMORE CRIMINALITY Notably, Humphrey's comment was not only tongue-in-cheek, but was not racist or prejudiced toward any group. It was not encouraging violence or other bad conduct. On the contrary, it implied criticism of those who continue to endanger others in the city. Yet, Minter went public with the virtue-signaling suspension. WIFE OF RAVENS OFFENSIVE LINEMAN APOLOGIZES MULTIPLE TIMES AFTER BACKLASH FOR CALLING BALTIMORE 'SCARY' One can only wonder whether the suspension would have happened if the Ravens were not on a dismal five-game losing streak, ranked fourth in the AFC North, and 11th in the AFC playoff rankings. We have previously discussed how players are not entitled to protest on the field in relation to the kneeling demonstrations. The same rule applies to other employees from Starbucks to Whole Foods. Employers are allowed to limit political expression and protests in the workplace. COLIN KAEPERNICK IS RIGHT ABOUT THE NFL'S 'PERFORMATIVE' RACISM CAMPAIGN — BUT HE'S ALSO A HYPOCRITE Companies also may contractually subject employees to discipline for public comments or actions that bring controversy or disrepute to the company. However, that does not make this right. I was critical of kneeling demonstrations during games, but I fully supported players' right to voice their views outside the game. NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS The NFL is notorious for hypocrisy and inconsistency in punishing free speech. The Humphrey controversy is reminiscent of the Commanders hammering a coach for expressing a different view of January 6. The NFL has spent years virtue-signaling with statements on helmets and in the end zones. However, when players or coaches express opposing views, they are silenced or suspended. NFL TOLD AZEEZ AL-SHAAIR HE'D BE PULLED FROM TEXANS GAME OVER PRO-PALESTINIAN EYEBLACK MESSAGE The NBA is little better. LeBron James can show disrespect to the National Anthem, but Jaden Ivy was fired for expressing his opposition to Pride Month. Players are expected to engage in mandatory speech while remaining silent on their own views. Nevertheless, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott rejected an apology by Humphrey: "While we acknowledge Marlon’s apology, a verbal apology is not enough." He added that Baltimore is "a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives." TEXANS' AZEEZ AL-SHAAIR TO BE FINED ONCE AGAIN BY NFL FOR WEARING PRO-PALESTINIAN PERSONAL MESSAGE ON EYEBLACK That is a curious objection, since Humphrey was highlighting the failure of Scott to make the city safe to protect those lives, given its top-five ranking for criminal violence. The message is clear. Players are expected to wear and repeat approved views of the team. For the NFL, speech codes reflect whatever values are popular or approved by NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and team owners. CARDINALS BACKUP CORNERBACK FINED BY NFL FOR WRITING 'GLORY BE 2 GOD' ON HIS EYEBLACK Now players are on notice that they cannot comment on blue cities being breeding grounds for crime. It is a curious sensitivity for a sport that often sounds like a gangbanger's delight from shotgun and pistol formations. The NFL and teams should get out of the speech regulation business and focus on football. While they are private companies and not directly subject to First Amendment limits, that does not mean that there are no free speech values at issue in these controversies. JONATHAN TURLEY: FRANCE'S FREE SPEECH CRACKDOWN SHOWS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN POLITICIANS DEFINE TRUTH The First Amendment is not the full or exclusive embodiment of free speech. It addresses just one of the dangers to free speech posed by government regulation. Many of us view free speech as a human right. Corporate censorship of social media clearly impacts free speech, and replacing Big Brother with a cadre of Little Brothers actually allows for far greater control of free expression. Humphrey has now issued the perfunctory apology and is publicly covering himself with sackcloth and ashes. While Baltimore can no longer be called "best at making criminals," the NFL certainly remains the best in coercing silence. articles.title: Princeton PhD student, Chinese-born neuroscientist, Eva Yi Xie detained by ICE at airport; DHS says she overstayed visa, lawyers challenge arrest
articles.summary: A 24-year-old Princeton University doctoral student has been detained by ICE after she was stopped at an airport while returning from an academic
articles.body: A 24-year-old Princeton University doctoral student has been detained by ICE after she was stopped at an airport while returning from an academic conference in Washington, DC. The Trump administration accused her of overstaying her visa, while her lawyers argued that she was legally allowed to remain in the US because of her pending asylum application. Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience PhD student at Princeton, was detained on November 19 at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Virginia. She had travelled to Washington to attend the Society for Neuroscience's annual conference, where she presented her research.The DHS said ICE had conducted a targeted enforcement operation at the airport to arrest Xie. According to the department, Xie entered the US on March 16, 2016, on a temporary basis and was required to leave by September 15, 2016. DHS alleged that she failed to depart by that date and did not have valid authorisation to study in the country."Xie will receive due process and remain in ICE custody pending her removal proceedings," the department said.However, her legal team has disputed the government's position, arguing that Xie has a pending asylum application that allows her to remain in the US while her case is being considered.Who is Eva Yi Xie?Xie moved to the US from China in 2016, when she was a minor. She attended the Bronx High School of Science in New York before graduating from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 2024 with degrees in computer science and mathematics. She joined Princeton University in 2024 and is a third-year doctoral candidate at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute. Her research focuses on the neural basis of decision-making, examining how the human brain processes information and makes choices. She is advised by Princeton neuroscience professor Carlos Brody and co-advised by professors Nathaniel Daw and Benjamin Eysenbach.Before joining Princeton, Xie also interned with Meta, Microsoft AI and IBM Research, according to The Daily Princetonian.Why was the Princeton student detained by ICE?Xie's lawyer, Kerry Doyle, told The Daily Princetonian that she was an asylum seeker whose immigration court hearing was scheduled for January 2028. Her family had applied for asylum within a year of arriving in the US, Doyle said. The application was referred to immigration court, where it remains pending. Although Xie's visa had expired, her lawyers claimed that her pending asylum application allowed her to stay in the country. They also said she had valid employment authorization and no criminal history.The lawyers have filed a habeas corpus petition in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, challenging the legality of her detention.According to Doyle, the petition argued that ICE arrested Xie without a warrant and that there were no circumstances suggesting she posed an imminent flight risk or needed to be taken into custody without one.A federal judge ordered ICE not to remove Xie from the Eastern District of Virginia before ruling on the habeas corpus petition. The agency was directed to respond to the petition by Wednesday, November 25.Princeton university arranges legal assistancePrinceton University confirmed that it had arranged legal representation for Xie following her detention. "News of Eva's detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community," Graduate School Dean Rodney Priestley said in a statement. He added that the university would remain in contact with her legal team, family and colleagues to provide support. "We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton," he said.Her research adviser, Carlos Brody, also appealed for help, describing her as a brilliant scientist, colleague, mentor and friend. "She went to a conference to present her work, and now she's in a detention center. She should be home," he wrote in a social media post.What happened before her arrest?Xie had travelled to Washington to attend the Society for Neuroscience's annual meeting and presented a research poster on November 18. She was reportedly preparing to board a domestic flight to San Francisco when she was detained the following day. A member of her research lab said Xie sent a message to colleagues on Slack asking for help on November 19. They lost contact with her for several hours before managing to reach her again.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.
articles.body:
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.

The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."

The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said that the Finnish Border Guard were responsible for the investigation into the attack and were co-operating with other relevant authorities.

Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry said.

The Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.

articles.title: Thousands of bags were stuck at airports as passengers urged to track luggage, pack lighter
articles.summary: Travel experts say AirTag luggage tracker and airline app alerts can protect checked bags after the Federal Aviation Administration halted flights nationwide recently.
articles.body: Travelers whose flights were disrupted by last week's nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop faced another headache once they finally landed. They didn't know if their checked bags made it to their destination. At Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas, for instance, hundreds of unclaimed bags remained in the terminal Monday after the Friday ground stop halted air travel across the U.S. for more than four hours, the Austin American-Statesman reported. Airport officials say excess baggage is common after widespread flight disruptions, as airlines work to reunite travelers with their belongings. 20,000 BAGS STRANDED AFTER TECHNICAL ISSUE AT MAJOR AIRPORT LEAVES TRAVELERS SCRAMBLING But travel experts said there are several things people can do to reduce the risk of luggage mix-ups and prepare in case it does happen, especially during the busy holiday travel season. If your checked bag doesn't arrive, checking an airline's app is a smart first step, Florida-based travel advisor Whytney Rawls told Fox News Digital. She recommended downloading the apps for airlines you fly and turning on notifications so you can follow updates and contact the carrier through the app. "It will help you keep everything organized and in order, especially if something goes wrong because they’re going to send the updates to that app," said Rawls, founder of The Amara Escapes and an advisor with Fora Travel. Rawls also suggested keeping baggage claim receipts and tag information handy. Take photos of the receipts and tags, too, she said, so identifying details are easy to find if a bag goes missing. US WARNS AMERICANS IN KEY LOCATIONS TO 'KEEP A LOW PROFILE' AHEAD OF CROWDED HOLIDAY TRAVEL A luggage tracker such as an AirTag can also help travelers see where their bags are, she said. "That is really important," Rawls said. She suggested using one in each bag. For those who check luggage, she said it's wise to pack as much clothing as possible in the carry-on, using vacuum-sealed bags to save space and wearing bulky items such as boots or a jacket, even when departing from a warm-weather destination, to free up space in the bag. "That'll get you much more space for things that you need to travel with on the plane," she said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "Get travel-size toiletries," she also said. Taking extra precautions is especially key when connecting flights are involved, Rawls noted. Cheryl Nelson, a Virginia-based FEMA-certified natural disaster and travel preparedness expert and founder of Prepare With Cher, recently experienced how quickly a routine trip can turn into an overnight stay. Delayed while trying to fly from San Francisco, she missed her Atlanta connection to Norfolk by five minutes and spent the night near the airport without her checked bag. Her luggage arrived the next morning. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES "I like to tell people to think of your carry-on as your insurance policy for a disrupted travel day," Nelson told Fox News Digital. "Don’t pack something in your checked bag that you absolutely need or couldn’t easily replace." She recommended keeping medications, glasses, valuables, electronics and chargers, basic toiletries, snacks and a change of clothes with you. "Don’t pack something in your checked bag that you absolutely need or couldn’t easily replace," she said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Before checking a suitcase, Nelson advised removing old airline tags to limit any confusion about where the bag is headed and adding a distinctive tag or ribbon to identify common-looking luggage. She also recommended allowing extra time for connections when possible. Tight layovers leave little margin for delays, gate changes or long taxi times, she said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Travel preparedness isn’t about expecting everything to go wrong," Nelson said. "It’s about having a few things with you that make a stressful situation a whole lot easier when it does." Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

articles.title: Friday night's win over Duke didn't prove Dabo Swinney is safe at Clemson, it did the opposite
articles.summary: Dabo Swinney's 20-10 win over Duke may have sealed his Clemson Tigers fate, echoing Jimbo Fisher and Billy Napier's late exits from college football.
articles.body: The discussions surrounding Dabo Swinney's job security as the head coach of the Clemson Tigers have reached a fever pitch. The two-time national championship winner has fallen on hard times recently, going from perennial College Football Playoff contender to ACC also-ran. Things appeared to have bottomed out this season, as the Tigers limped into their Friday night showdown with Duke holding a 6-4 record and having little offense to speak of in 2026. DABO SWINNEY REACTS AFTER CLEMSON HITS LATEST LOW WITH UPSET LOSS TO GEORGIA TECH: 'NOBODY COMING TO SAVE US' The noise regarding Dabo and his future at Clemson was only getting louder, but, miraculously, the Tigers took care of business and beat the Blue Devils 20-10 on the road. You would think this data point would show Swinney is looking to end this season on a high note and head into 2027 with some momentum and that maybe this was his first step towards saving his job. That isn't news to anyone who has been following the sport for the past several years (or to anyone who has read any of my articles on the guy). What you may find shocking is this win over Duke may actually be a sign that Dabo is all but officially done at Clemson. Much like a dying dog who gets a last burst of energy before taking a turn, it's quite common for lame duck head coaches to go out and get one last big win before exiting stage left. These kinds of things happen all the time, especially in power conferences with high-profile coaches. Last year, Billy Napier was surely on his way out of Gainesville when his 1-3 Florida Gators took down a top-ten Texas team in The Swamp. Jimbo Fisher was famously fired following a blowout win over Mississippi State in 2023, holding the same 6-4 record that Clemson had heading into its game Friday night. articles.title: Maher calls out 'spoiled brats' who left US over Trump presidency, says country ‘self-corrected’ in midterms
articles.summary: Bill Maher mocked the "spoiled brats" who fled to England or Ireland over Trump, questioning the patriotism of stars who left after losing elections.
articles.body: Bill Maher, host of HBO's "Real Time," took a swipe at liberals who fled the country over President Donald Trump’s administration, calling them "spoiled brats" as he celebrated Democrats’ sweep in this month’s midterm elections. Speaking to the audience during the show’s season finale Friday night, Maher blasted Democrats who moved abroad following Trump’s election victories in 2016 and 2024. "But it is also important to remember to mock and ridicule the spoiled brats who fled to England or Ireland because America was so irredeemably ‘Trumpian-Republican,’" Maher said as he flashed a news headline highlighting "21 celebs who fled the U.S. amid Trump’s presidency." AMERICANS WHO MOVED TO EUROPE AFTER TRUMP WIN NOW SAY THEY REGRET LEAVING "Only to come back to America now because America did what America does: self-corrected," he added. Maher went on to question the judgment of those who left their country over election results that they were unhappy with, as he touted Democrats’ historic sweep in the midterm election earlier this month. NEW YORK TIMES GLEEFUL OVER DEMOCRATS' HUGE MIDTERM VICTORIES, SAYS IT'S TIME TO ‘FEEL PRIDE’ "You left the country you're supposed to love forever because you lost an election or two, and now you look like the husband who leaves his wife because she let herself go for a while," Maher added. "Well, guess what? We got hot again." Maher began by making fun of conservatives who left blue states: "Let's all allow ourselves a good laugh at the people who uprooted their whole lives in blue states to move to red states that are now blue states." He praised the results of the midterms, noting, "We should all have a little more faith that democracy can still do its thing. And it's a beautiful thing. The sound of a country turning the page, catching up with its own ideals." The HBO host's comments come after several high-profile celebrities — including comedians Rosie O’Donnell and Ellen DeGeneres — cited Trump’s election victory as their driving force for moving abroad. ROSIE O'DONNELL HAMMERS TRUMP REPEATEDLY IN KIMMEL GUEST-HOST GIG AS WHITE HOUSE FIRES BACK "We got here the day before the election and woke up to lots of texts from our friends with crying emojis, and I was like, 'He got in,'" DeGeneres told broadcaster Richard Bacon after she and her wife, Portia de Rossi, decided to relocate to the United Kingdom, according to the BBC in 2025. "And we're like, 'We're staying here.'" O’Donnell referred to Trump as "Mango Mussolini" on the Aug. 17 episode of "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" during a week-long guest-hosting stint that brought the 64-year-old comic back to the United States from her new home in Ireland. ART GARFUNKEL JOINS GROWING LIST OF CELEBRITIES CONSIDERING A MOVE ABROAD OVER TRUMP PRESIDENCY "I read that Project 2025 and said, ‘Got to get myself out of here, you know,’ and I decided to go to Ireland, a place where people are driven to drink regardless of who's running their country," O’Donnell said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Musician Art Garfunkel also weighed the possibility of leaving the United States over Trump’s presidency, telling The Guardian earlier this year that he is unhappy with the administration’s handling of climate change, international affairs and other political issues. "I don’t like America’s position at all," he told the outlet. "I’m not on board, and I’m thinking of leaving the country, frankly." articles.title: Zelenskyy says Russia strikes hometown, criticizes Putin-Trump meeting
articles.summary: Zelenskyy says a Russian strike on his hometown Kryvyi Rih killed two people, including 7-year-old Tykhon, and wounded 58 others in a civilian area.
articles.body: A Russian strike on Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 58 others, the Ukrainian leader said Saturday. A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday night in the central Ukraine town, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration. Zelenkskyy said in a social media post the woman was an emergency medical worker and the boy was named Tykhon. PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE "He was born in 2019, and, sadly, most of his life was lived during a war like this. And the Russians took his life with their strike. My condolences to their families and loved ones," Zelenkskyy said. On top of the civilian deaths and injuries, the strike sparked four fires and damaged roughly 25 apartment buildings, along with a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, businesses and vehicles. RUSSIA'S PUTIN VOWS A RESPONSE 'FAR MORE PAINFUL' AFTER UKRAINE ATTACKS PRIZED BRIDGE IN CRIMEA Zelenkskyy claimed that the Russian strike hit an area of the city with no military targets. "The strike hit an ordinary civilian area of the city – there are no military facilities nearby, and there never have been," he wrote, adding, "Russia is waging war against life, and there can be NO justification for this." TRUMP WILL FACE REPORTERS AFTER HISTORIC XI-PUTIN TALKS AS WAR QUESTIONS LINGER The Ukrainian leader later commented on President Donald Trump's recent trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. "Putin didn't get his 'Yalta 2,'" Zelenskyy wrote, referring to the famed 1945 Yalta Conference between former U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin. TRUMP’S PROPOSED RUSSIA DEAL RAISES NATO ALARM AS EX-COMMANDER WARNS PUTIN SEEKS INFLUENCE OVER EUROPE "As far as I understand, he recently commented: 'What's wrong with Yalta? Those were the victories over Nazism, over fascism, and so on, that were sealed there.' First of all, indeed, this was no Yalta. Did Putin want a real Yalta? Yes. In the sense of carving up the world and changing borders. China didn't let itself be drawn into it. I don't know what happened between the United States and Russia in their bilateral, but Ukraine wasn't discussed. Nothing came out publicly. So the redrawing of borders didn't happen," Zelenskyy wrote. "If there really was an intention to reaffirm the victory over fascism now, then the participants at this summit would have to be the United States, Europe, and Ukraine. Definitely not Russia. I think this trilateral summit turned out very badly for Russia. Not only did Putin fail to get the results he wanted, but we also saw his reaction. "And, unfortunately, we saw that reaction in Ukraine. There was a massive attack that night – 111 missiles. If Putin wanted to remind the world once again who he is, there was no need – we haven't forgotten that he's a terrorist and a killer," his X post continued. UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY' The strike on Zelenskyy's hometown is far from uncommon, with periodic Russian attacks targeting the industrial steel town dozens of times since the start of the war in 2022. The incident also occurred as a Russian ship was struck by drones on Saturday, causing it to catch fire in the Gulf of Finland. The Russian-flagged Sparta II was struck by a drone shortly before 9 a.m. local time, according to Finnish Coast Guard Commander Mikko Simola. "Generally it should be noted that it is known that this Sparta II vessel has been used for transports for the Russian state, including the armed forces," Simola said. As a result of its damage, the craft entered Finnish territorial waters. Simola also noted that Finland believed a Russian helicopter crossed Finland's sovereign borders as well. Finnish officials believe that Ukraine was behind the attack. "It is likely that Ukraine ... is behind (the attack)," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen said. articles.title: The medallion's modern appeal
articles.summary: Explore the captivating world of medallion jewelry, its historical significance, and how it's making waves in contemporary fashion, reflecting individuality and style.
articles.body: Suddenly, the medallion is everywhere — from jewellery pieces to make-up boxes and holiday treats. A recent example is Zendaya’s controversial 3,000-year-old gold medallion plaque earrings she wore at a London promotion event for The Odyssey film in July 2026. They were believed to have originally been found in northwestern Iran.Independent designers and established fashion houses have also been incorporating the medallion into their collections in varied ways for quite some time now. Dior, for instance, has been using its iconic Dior Médaillon in beauty product packaging, holiday campaigns featuring medallion-shaped tree ornaments and gingerbread biscuits, and bag and belt buckles.Other fashion houses, including Celine, Gabriela Hearst, Missoni, Vivetta and Nina Ricci, have explored the motif through medallion belts, long-chain necklaces, earrings and statement belt buckles in their Spring/Summer 2026-27 collections.The motif has also found favour with high jewellery maisons such as De Beers, Van Cleef & Arpels and Chanel, which have incorporated this architectural form into their 2025 and 2026 collections.A medallion is a round, flat ornamentIt is a historical motif that held significant value for ancient civilisations and was used as military honours, political currency, religious relics and artistic objects. Biren Vaidya, jewellery designer, managing director and creative head, The Rose Group of Companies, tells us, “From ancient Indian coins to Greek and Roman medallions, these objects have traditionally represented power, faith, prosperity and remembrance. They often featured portraits of rulers and deities, or symbols that held particular significance for those who wore them."Today, it has evolved into jewellery, belt buckles, keychains, hair clips, decorative bag clasps and more.Choose a medallion that you feel naturally drawn to. It could be the symbolism or the craftsmanship. Consider its proportion, wearability, weight, length and style of the chain. Prioritise craftsmanship on both sides. A beautifully finished reverse indicates the attention invested in the pieceWide scope for experimentationThe beauty of a medallion lies in the freedom it offers a designer, says Vaidya. When it comes to metal and materials used to make the medallion, he says, “Gold will always have a special place in this kind of jewellery for engraving, embossing and intricate relief work, allowing the craftsmanship to become an integral part of the design.” However, the medallion also offers the opportunity to introduce other materials and textures. “Diamonds, coloured gemstones, enamel and ornamental stones offer wonderful possibilities.”What makes it appealingThe medallion is not just a piece of jewellery. Madhuri Singh, a celebrity fashion stylist, believes it reflects individuality. “People are moving beyond choosing jewellery purely for its decorative appeal. The medallion’s resurgence reflects a larger shift towards jewellery that has character, meaning and a story to tell.”Timelessness too makes it special. Vaidya highlights, “It is one of those rare forms of jewellery that has remained relevant across centuries, despite changing fashions and tastes. Much of that enduring appeal comes from its ability to hold meaning. Over time, its significance often extends beyond the metal and craftsmanship and gets associated with memories and relationships.”The artwork is also central to the identity of a medallion. Akanksha Arora, CEO, Tribe Amrapali, tells us, “A medallion offers a canvas for storytelling. The motif gives the piece its personality and can make it meaningful to the wearer beyond its aesthetic appeal. We are seeing an interesting mix of interpretations, from traditional floral and architectural references to celestial symbols, spiritual motifs and more contemporary graphic designs. Personalisation is also adding another dimension, with people gravitating towards symbols that reflect their beliefs, memories or individual identities.”What makes it particularly relevant today is its versatility. “A medallion,” says Arora, “can be worn as a standalone statement with contemporary clothing, layered with finer chains for a more relaxed look, or paired with traditional jewellery for festive and occasion dressing.”The medallion has remained relevant across generations because it is rooted in something more enduring than fashion trends. It brings together history, personal expression and contemporary design in a form that can remain meaningful well beyond a particular trendIndia has been making its medallions for centuriesIndia has a rich tradition of medallion and coin-style jewellery. According to Vaidya, many of the forms we associate with contemporary medallion jewellery have existed in India for centuries. “The Kasu Mala of South India, with its distinctive gold coin motifs, is a wonderful example. Temple jewellery also features beautifully rendered circular pendants depicting deities, while gold mohurs or seals and taweez worn across different communities are other interesting examples. Contemporary medallion jewellery is, in many ways, a continuation of these traditional pieces, interpreted through a more modern design language.”How to wear your medallionBesides just a neck chain, a medallion can be explored through statement earrings, oversized rings, cuffs, bracelets and broochesExperiment with layered chains featuring medallions of different sizes or use a statement brooch or belt buckle to incorporate the motif more subtlyTreat the medallion as a focal point and not as just another accessory. A simple T-shirt, a plain dress or a minimal silhouette is often all you need to let the jewellery do the talking.For occasion wear, you can experiment with oversized medallions and sculptural designs. Try an oversized medallion reinterpreted as a bra top or even a sculpted corset. It becomes wearable art rather than just an accessoryA medallion can look particularly interesting with an open-neck shirt, a sheer shirt or even a slightly unbuttoned, relaxed silhouette, where the jewellery becomes visible against the skin(As suggested by Madhuri Singh, celebrity fashion stylist)You use AI every day.
